definition_zh: 相等的；平等的；同等的人；等于
definition_en: the same in amount, value, or status, or to be the same as something
core_image: 天平两端放着同样重的东西，横杆保持水平
scene: 两根绳子长度相同，承受的重量也一样。 The two ropes are equal in length and strength.
sceneCN: 这里 equal 是「相等的」（第 1 个义项：在数量或程度上相同）；句意：两根绳子的长度和强度都相同。

senses.title: The same in amount or degree
senses.definition: having the same size, amount, value, or level as something else
senses.definitionCN: 在大小、数量、价值或水平上与他人或他物相同
senses.example: Cut the cake into eight equal pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 把蛋糕切成八块大小相等的份。
senses.why: Latin aequalis means level or even, so equal first describes things that balance perfectly.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aequalis 意为水平、均匀，所以 equal 首先描述完全平衡的事物。

senses.title: Having the same rights or status
senses.definition: having the same rights, opportunities, or treatment as others
senses.definitionCN: 与其他人拥有相同的权利、机会或待遇
senses.example: Every citizen deserves equal treatment under the law.
senses.exampleCN: 每位公民在法律面前都应得到平等对待。
senses.why: The idea of an even balance extends from weights and amounts to people and their rights.
senses.whyCN: 「平衡」的概念从重量和数量扩展到人及其权利。

senses.title: A person of the same rank
senses.definition: a person who has the same ability, rank, or status as another
senses.definitionCN: 能力、地位或身份与另一人相同的人
senses.example: She treats her students as her equals.
senses.exampleCN: 她把学生当作与自己平等的人。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for someone who stands on the same level.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转化为名词，指站在同一水平上的人。

senses.title: To be the same as
senses.definition: to be the same in amount or value as something, or to match it
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或价值上等同于某物，或与之匹敌
senses.example: Two plus three equals five.
senses.exampleCN: 二加三等于五。
senses.why: The verb turns the balanced relation into an action of matching.
senses.whyCN: 动词把平衡关系转化为「相配、等同」的动作。

intro.en: Equal comes from Latin aequalis, uniform or even, from aequus, level or fair.
intro.cn: equal 来自拉丁语 aequalis（均匀、相等），源于 aequus（平的、公平的）。

items.en: Aequus means level, even, or fair.
items.cn: aequus 意为平的、均匀的、公平的。

items.en: Aequalis means uniform or of the same age.
items.cn: aequalis 意为均匀的或同年的。

items.en: Equal carries the sense of even and alike.
items.cn: equal 带有「平、相同」的含义。

items.en: Equal covers amounts and the rights of people.
items.cn: 中古英语 equal 涵盖数量与人的权利。

items.en: Modern English adds the noun for a person of the same rank.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了表示同等之人的名词用法。

note.en: Equal is a balance word with a large family and a set of near words for sameness.
note.cn: equal 是表示「平衡」的词，拥有庞大词族，并与表示相同的一组词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Equal comes from a level root: two sides of a scale sitting perfectly even.
normalIntro.cn: equal 来自「水平」的词根：天平两边完全齐平。

normal.en: Equal parts means every part is the same size.
normal.cn: equal parts 指每一份大小相同。

normal.en: Equal rights means the same rights for everyone.
normal.cn: equal rights 指人人拥有相同权利。

normal.en: The verb equals appears in arithmetic.
normal.cn: 动词 equals 出现在算术中。

normal.en: Equality is the noun for the equal state.
normal.cn: equality 是表示平等状态的名词。

normal.en: Compare identical: identical is stricter, equal allows different forms of the same value.
normal.cn: 对比 identical：identical 更严格，equal 允许同一价值的不同形式。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with two identical weights.
abstract.cn: 想象一台天平两端放着相同的砝码。

abstract.en: Imagine eight cake slices cut by a careful hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手仔细切出八块相同的蛋糕。

abstract.en: Think of two runners crossing a line at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两名跑者同时冲过终点线。

examples.en: The two teams finished with equal scores.
examples.cn: 两支队伍最终得分相同。

examples.en: The law promises equal pay for equal work.
examples.cn: 法律承诺同工同酬。

examples.en: One kilometer equals a thousand meters.
examples.cn: 一公里等于一千米。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e + qual」——两边一样平，就是相等；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（平的、公平的）→ aequalis（均匀的）→ 古法语 equal → 英语 equal，核心义「两端齐平、彼此相同」。

sensesIntro.en: Equal starts with even amounts, extends to fair treatment, then to a person of the same standing, and finally to the verb of matching.
sensesIntro.cn: equal 从数量相等开始，扩展到公平对待，再指地位相同的人，最后成为表示「等于」的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale perfectly level on both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平两边完全水平。

branches.en: Even amount is the basic measurable sense.
branches.cn: 数量相等是基本的可测量义项。

branches.en: Fair treatment extends balance to rights.
branches.cn: 公平对待把平衡扩展到权利。

branches.en: A peer is a person on the same level.
branches.cn: 同等之人是站在同一水平上的人。

branches.en: The verb states that two things match.
branches.cn: 动词陈述两事物彼此相等。

branches.en: Equal shares and equal rights both rest on the same balance.
branches.cn: 均分与平权都建立在同一种平衡之上。

intro.en: Equal is a Latin fairness word, and English builds equality, equally, and equate around it.
intro.cn: equal 是拉丁语中表示公平的词，英语围绕它构成 equality、equally 与 equate。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus means level and fair, and aequalis means even or uniform.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 意为平的、公平的，aequalis 意为均匀的。

definition_zh: 砰的一声；猛击；刘海
definition_en: a sudden loud noise, a hard hit, or hair cut straight across the forehead
core_image: 门被风一吹，砰地撞上门框
scene: 楼道里的窗户没关。 The door closed with a loud bang.
sceneCN: 这里 bang 是「砰的一声」（第 1 个义项：突然的巨响）；句意是门砰的一声关上了。

derivatives.zh: 由 bang 加 -er 构成，义为「爆竹；旧车」
由 bang 加 -ing 构成，义为「砰砰的敲击声」

senses.title: A sudden loud noise
senses.definition: a short, very loud noise like a gun or a slammed door
senses.definitionCN: 像枪响或关门那样短促而巨大的声音
senses.example: The door closed with a loud bang.
senses.exampleCN: 门砰的一声关上了。
senses.why: Bang is an imitative word, shaped to sound like the noise it names.
senses.whyCN: bang 是拟声词，读音就是模仿它所指的声音。

senses.title: A hard hit
senses.definition: to hit something hard or to close it noisily
senses.definitionCN: 用力击打某物或把它砰地关上
senses.example: He banged the box on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 他把箱子砰地砸在地上。
senses.why: A loud impact makes a bang, so the verb came to mean hitting something with force.
senses.whyCN: 巨大的撞击会发出砰声，所以动词就表示用力撞击。

senses.title: Hair over the forehead
senses.definition: hair cut straight across the forehead
senses.definitionCN: 齐齐剪在额头前的头发
senses.example: She cut her bangs short before the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出行前她把刘海剪短了。
senses.why: This sense probably comes from the idea of a cut edge, and it is mainly American English.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项可能来自「剪齐的边缘」这一想法，主要见于美式英语。

intro.en: Bang began as a word that imitates a loud noise.

definition_zh: 前景；可能性；景象；潜在客户；勘探；展望
definition_en: the view ahead, whether seen by the eye or expected by the mind, and the act of searching the ground for what it may hold
core_image: 一个人站在高处向前看，视线越过地平线，既看见眼前的景，也看见将要发生的事
scene: 年轻工程师站在黎明的山脊上，望着可能蕴藏矿藏的谷地。 The prospect of finding copper in this valley is good.
sceneCN: 这里 prospect 是「可能性、机会」（第 2 个义项：某事将会发生或成功的可能性）；句意：这里找到铜的可能性很大，但他宁愿过安稳日子。画面里有山脊、晨雾和尚未开挖的谷地；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 前景；可能性；景象；潜在客户

collocations.zh: 有前途的人选/潜在客户

derivatives.zh: （学校、企业的）章程；招股说明书

senses.title: The future in view: what lies ahead
senses.titleCN: 前景：前方等待的那幅图景
senses.definition: the possibility or expectation of something happening in the future, especially something good
senses.definitionCN: 对未来某事的可能性或预期，尤指好事
senses.example: The prospect of a long winter worried the farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长冬季的前景让农民们忧心。
senses.why: The noun appears in the 1660s as 'expectation, ground of expectation', from the habit of looking forward. What the eye does in space, the mind does in time: it scans the horizon of coming events.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词在 17 世纪 60 年代出现，义为“预期、期待的依据”，来自“向前看”的动作。眼睛在空间里做的事，心智在时间里也做：它扫视将要发生之事的地平线。

senses.title: A chance that may come true
senses.titleCN: 可能性、机会：尚未兑现的那份可能
senses.definition: a chance or possibility that something will happen or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 某事将会发生或成功的可能性
senses.example: There is little prospect of finding survivors after so long.
senses.exampleCN: 过了这么久，找到幸存者的可能性很小。
senses.why: The 1620s sense 'mental view or survey' let people speak of viewing a future outcome. Once an outcome is 'in view', it is a chance on the horizon rather than a certainty in hand.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 20 年代“心中的审视”这一义项，让人可以“看见”未来的结果。一个结果一旦“在视野里”，它就是地平线上的机会，而不是握在手里的确定。

senses.title: The sweep of the eye: a wide view
senses.titleCN: 景象、视野：眼睛扫过的那一大片
senses.definition: a view or scene, especially a wide one seen from a high place
senses.definitionCN: 景色、景象，尤指从高处看到的广阔视野
senses.example: From the hilltop we had a fine prospect of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 从山顶上，我们看到了山谷的美丽景色。
senses.why: From 1530s English, prospect meant 'extensive view of the landscape', straight from Latin prospectus 'distant view'. The word still carries the physical sweep of the eye before it carries hope.
senses.whyCN: 从 16 世纪 30 年代起，prospect 指“广阔的风景视野”，直接来自拉丁语 prospectus“远处的景色”。这个词先有眼睛的物理扫视，后才有希望之义。

senses.title: Someone worth watching: the promising person
senses.titleCN: 潜在客户、有前途的人选：值得盯住的那个人
senses.definition: a person or thing seen as likely to succeed, or a possible customer or candidate
senses.definitionCN: 被认为可能成功的人或事物；潜在客户或候选人
senses.example: The agent spends her mornings calling new prospects.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经纪人每天上午给新潜在客户打电话。
senses.why: From 1922, prospect named 'a person or thing considered promising', out of the 1660s sense of expectation of advantage. A good customer is someone in whom the seller sees a future.
senses.whyCN: 从 1922 年起，prospect 指“被认为有前途的人或事物”，源自 17 世纪 60 年代“预期好处”的义项。好客户，就是卖方在其身上看得见未来的人。

senses.title: Grounds for hoping
senses.titleCN: 预期的依据：凭什么盼着
senses.definition: grounds for expecting something; a reasonable basis for anticipation
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的预期依据；合理的盼望理由
senses.example: The deal offers no prospect of profit this year.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔交易今年没有获利的指望。
senses.why: The 1660s sense was not the hope itself but its ground: 'expectation, ground of expectation'. The landscape metaphor persists — a prospect is what the situation lets you see coming.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 60 年代的义项不是希望本身，而是希望的依据：“预期、期待的依据”。风景的隐喻仍在：prospect 就是局势允许你看见的、即将到来的东西。

senses.title: Looking for ore: to prospect the ground
senses.definition: to search an area for gold, oil, or other minerals
senses.definitionCN: 在某地区寻找黄金、石油或其他矿藏
senses.example: They prospected the valley for copper throughout the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天他们都在那个山谷里勘探铜矿。
senses.why: The verb dates from 1841, from a specialized 1832 noun sense 'a spot giving prospects of ore'. The miner literally looks out over the land to see what it promises.
senses.whyCN: 动词始于 1841 年，来自 1832 年的名词专义“有矿苗的地方”。矿工字面上就是在土地上四处张望，看它许诺了什么。

senses.title: Surveying the site before building
senses.titleCN: 勘察、探测：动工之前先看一遍
senses.definition: to examine land or a site, especially to judge its potential or value
senses.definitionCN: 勘查土地或场地，尤指评估其潜力或价值
senses.example: Engineers prospected the site before the dam was approved.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝获批之前，工程师们勘察了坝址。
senses.why: English had an older verb prospect 'look forth, look out over' (1550s) from Latin prospectare, a frequentative of prospicere. The mining sense revived that old surveying gesture.
senses.whyCN: 英语早有动词 prospect“向外看、俯瞰”（16 世纪 50 年代），来自拉丁语 prospectare，是 prospicere 的反复体。采矿义让这个古老的勘看动作重新流行。

senses.title: A mental survey: the wide view of a subject
senses.titleCN: 宏观审视：把一门学问摊开来看
senses.definition: a broad mental view or survey of a subject, situation, or period
senses.definitionCN: 对某一主题、局势或时期的宏观心理审视
senses.example: The book gives a broad prospect of a century of science.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书对百年科学史作了宏观的审视。
senses.why: The transferred sense 'mental view or survey' is recorded from the 1620s. The eye's sweep over a valley becomes the mind's sweep over a field of knowledge.
senses.whyCN: “心中的视野/审视”这一转移义记录于 17 世纪 20 年代。眼睛扫过山谷的动作，变成了心智扫过一片知识领域。

senses.title: The long straight avenue
senses.titleCN: 大街、大道：一眼望不到头的那条路
senses.definition: a wide, straight street or avenue, especially in a Russian city
senses.definitionCN: 宽阔笔直的大街或大道，尤指俄罗斯城市中的
senses.example: Nevsky Prospect runs straight through the heart of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 涅瓦大街笔直地穿过城市中心。
senses.why: In 1866 English borrowed Russian prospekt 'avenue', which itself came from Latin prospectus. A grand avenue is a street designed to give the eye a long, uninterrupted prospect.
senses.whyCN: 1866 年英语借入俄语 prospekt“大街”，而俄语这个词又来自拉丁语 prospectus。宏伟的大道，就是一条为了让视线获得漫长而不中断的前景而设计的街。

intro.en: Prospect is one of the spec- words: all of them are about looking. Latin prospicere 'look forward' gives the noun prospectus 'a distant view', and English extends the same word from landscape to expectation, to customers, and finally to mining.
intro.cn: prospect 是 spec- 词族的一员：它们都与“看”有关。拉丁语 prospicere“向前看”给出名词 prospectus“远处的景色”，英语再把同一个词从风景扩展到预期、客户，最后扩展到采矿。

items.en: Prospicere meant 'to look out on, look forward', built from pro 'forward' plus specere 'to look at'. Specere goes back to PIE *spek- 'to observe', a reconstruction with no written record, so that deepest layer is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: prospicere 意为“眺望、向前看”，由 pro“向前”加 specere“看”构成。specere 可追溯到印欧语 *spek-“观察”，但这是没有书面记录的重构，因此最深层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Prospectus, the past-participle stem used as a noun, meant 'distant view, look out; sight, faculty of sight'. It named both the thing seen and the power of seeing it.
items.cn: prospectus 由过去分词词干用作名词，意为“远处的景色、眺望；视觉、视力”。它既指被看见之物，也指看见的能力。

items.en: The noun enters English as 'the act of looking into the distance; the condition of facing something or a certain direction'. The looking is still literal.
items.cn: 名词进入英语时意为“向远处看的动作；朝向某物或某个方向的状态”。这里的“看”仍是字面义。

items.en: The meaning widens to 'an extensive view of the landscape' (1530s), then to 'mental view or survey' (1620s), then to 'that which is presented to the eye, a scene' (1630s).
items.cn: 词义先扩展为“广阔的风景视野”（16 世纪 30 年代），再扩展为“心中的审视”（17 世纪 20 年代），又扩展为“呈现于眼前之物、景象”（17 世纪 30 年代）。

items.en: 'Expectation, ground of expectation, especially of advantage' appears in the 1660s on the notion of looking forward. From it come 'person or thing considered promising' (1922) and the plural prospects, 'things looked forward to'.
items.cn: “预期、期待的依据，尤指好处”于 17 世纪 60 年代出现，基于“向前看”的意象。由此派生出“被认为有前途的人或事物”（1922）以及复数 prospects“所期待之事”。

items.en: Mining uses a specialized noun sense 'a spot giving prospects of ore' (1832), and the verb 'explore for gold or minerals' follows in 1841, from prospect (n.).
items.cn: 采矿业先有名词专义“有矿苗的地点”（1832），动词“勘探黄金或矿物”于 1841 年随后出现，来自名词 prospect。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the spec- look or the -spect shape; the meaning group shares the idea of a future chance, but not its spelling.
note.cn: 形近组共享 spec-“看”或 -spect 的外形；近义组共享“未来的机会”这一概念，但拼写不同。

entries.definition: a printed plan describing a school, company, or proposed enterprise. It is prospect plus the Latin noun ending -us.
entries.definitionCN: 介绍学校、公司或拟办事业的印刷章程。它就是 prospect 加上拉丁名词词尾 -us。

entries.definition: to look back at someone with esteem. It uses the same specere 'look' but with re- 'back'.
entries.definitionCN: 尊重；回头看某人并怀有敬意。它用同一个 specere“看”，但前缀是 re-“向后”。

entries.definition: a person who watches an event. The root is pure 'look', with no pro- 'forward'.
entries.definitionCN: 观众；旁观者。词根是纯粹的“看”，没有 pro-“向前”。

entries.definition: a way of seeing things from a particular point. It looks through a situation rather than forward.
entries.definitionCN: 视角；透视法。它是透过一个情境去看，而不是向前看。

entries.definition: the likely future of a situation. It is the closest everyday synonym of prospect in the sense of expectation.
entries.definitionCN: 前景；展望。在“预期”这一义项上，它是最接近 prospect 的日常同义词。

entries.definition: the chance that something will happen. It measures probability, while prospect often adds hope or dread.
entries.definitionCN: 可能性；或然性。它衡量概率，而 prospect 常带有希望或忧虑的色彩。

entries.definition: a long, wide view, especially between rows of trees. It matches the landscape sense of prospect.
entries.definitionCN: 远景；狭长的视野，尤指树列之间的。它对应 prospect 的风景义。

entries.definition: the act of expecting something and preparing for it. It names the mental act that prospect describes as a view.
entries.definitionCN: 预期；期待。它命名的是 prospect 以“视野”来描绘的那种心理活动。

entries.definition: something that may exist or happen. It is neutral, where prospect usually implies evaluation.
entries.definitionCN: 可能性；可能之事。它是中性的，而 prospect 通常含有评价意味。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin specere 'to look', the spec- family, and the mining and customer senses that grew from the same gaze.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 specere“看”、spec- 词族，以及从同一道目光里长出的采矿义和客户义。

normal.en: prospect = pro- 'forward' + spect 'look': to look forward is to see a prospect.
normal.cn: prospect = pro-“向前”+ spect“看”：向前看，看见的就是前景。

normal.en: The spec- family is all eyes: spectator, inspect, respect, perspective, circumspect.
normal.cn: spec- 词族全是眼睛：spectator、inspect、respect、perspective、circumspect。

normal.en: A prospectus is the same word in a brochure: a school lets you look ahead at what it offers.
normal.cn: prospectus 就是同一个词做成的小册子：学校让你提前看见它能提供什么。

normal.en: A prospector looks over the ground exactly as you look over the future.
normal.cn: prospector（勘探者）打量土地的样子，正像你打量未来。

normal.en: Job prospects are literally 'things looked forward to' in the plural.
normal.cn: job prospects 字面上就是复数形式的“被向前看的事情”。

abstract.en: Future is treated as a landscape: you stand here and scan what is coming.
abstract.cn: 未来被当作一片风景：你站在此处，扫视将要到来的一切。

abstract.en: Looking and hoping are one gesture in this word; the eye and the mind share a horizon.
abstract.cn: 在这个词里，看与盼是同一个动作；眼睛和心智共享一条地平线。

abstract.en: The word travels from landscape to time to market: a view, a chance, a customer.
abstract.cn: 这个词从风景走到时间，再走到市场：一片景、一个机会、一位客户。

examples.en: The prospect of moving abroad excited her more than it frightened her.
examples.cn: 移居国外的前景让她兴奋多过害怕。

examples.en: Geologists spent three years prospecting for oil in the desert.
examples.cn: 地质学家在沙漠里花了三年勘探石油。

examples.en: The sales team treats every inquiry as a potential prospect.
examples.cn: 销售团队把每一次询价都当作潜在客户。

dict_mnemonic.text: pro（向前）+ spect（看）——向前看，前景就在眼前；谐音“普罗斯佩克特”：普查（pro）一遍，向前看矿藏 → prospect 前景；勘探

root: 源自拉丁语 prospicere“向前看、眺望”，由 pro“向前”加 specere“看”构成，名词 prospectus 意为“远处的景色”；核心是“向前看所得到的那片景”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses, one gaze. The eye first sweeps a landscape, then the mind sweeps the future; what is seen becomes a chance, a customer, a subject surveyed, a street, and finally ground to be searched for ore.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项，一道目光。眼睛先扫过风景，心智再扫过未来；被看见的东西依次变成机会、客户、被审视的学科、一条大街，最后成为要去地下搜寻矿藏的土地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing high and looking forward — the view ahead, in space or in time.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在高处向前看——空间或时间中前方的那片景。

chain: SEE A CHANCE IN A PERSON

branches.en: THE EXPECTED FUTURE: prospect as what is anticipated, and the grounds for that anticipation.
branches.cn: 被期待的未来：作为预期内容的前景，以及支撑这份预期的依据。

branches.en: THE CHANCE AND THE PERSON: a possibility on the horizon, and someone in whom a future is seen.
branches.cn: 机会与人：地平线上的可能性，以及被人看见未来的人。

branches.en: THE WIDE VIEW: the landscape before the eyes, and the broad survey before the mind.
branches.cn: 广阔视野：眼前的风景，以及心智对学科的宏观审视。

branches.en: LOOKING INTO THE EARTH: mining for ore, and surveying a site for what it may yield.
branches.cn: 向地下看：探矿，以及为评估潜力而勘察场地。

branches.en: THE LONG AVENUE: a street built to give the eye an unbroken prospect.
branches.cn: 长长的大道：一条为了让视线获得不中断前景而建的街。

intro.en: Prospect is pro- plus spec- plus -t. Its family shows the prefix pro-, re-, per-, circum- and in-, the root spec- 'look', and the noun and agent endings -tus, -tor, -ive and -ion.
intro.cn: prospect 是 pro- 加 spec- 再加 -t。它的词族展示前缀 pro-、re-、per-、circum-、in-，词根 spec-“看”，以及名词与施事后缀 -tus、-tor、-ive、-ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere 'to look at' is the base of spectator, inspect and respect; with prefixes it yields prospicere, respicere, perspicere and circumspicere, and the noun prospectus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere“看”是 spectator、inspect、respect 的基础；加前缀又给出 prospicere、respicere、perspicere、circumspicere，以及名词 prospectus。

items.meaning: a view ahead; expectation; to search the ground
items.example: The prospect of promotion kept her working late.
items.exampleCN: 升职的前景让她一直工作到很晚。

items.example: Officials came to inspect the factory.
items.exampleCN: 官员们来检查这家工厂。

items.meaning: to look back at with esteem
items.example: Students respect a teacher who listens.
items.exampleCN: 学生尊敬愿意倾听的老师。

items.example: The stadium held fifty thousand spectators.
items.exampleCN: 体育场容纳了五万名观众。

items.meaning: a way of seeing through a scene
items.example: Travel gives you a new perspective on home.
items.exampleCN: 旅行让你对家乡有了新的视角。

items.meaning: to look out mentally; to guess or invest
items.example: Reporters speculated about the reason for her resignation.
items.exampleCN: 记者们推测她辞职的原因。

items.meaning: the side something presents to the eye
items.meaningCN: 方面；外观（看过去的那一面）
items.example: We discussed every aspect of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 我们讨论了计划的每个方面。

items.meaningCN: 谨慎的（四周看遍再行动）
items.example: She was circumspect in accepting the offer.
items.exampleCN: 她在接受这个提议时很谨慎。

items.meaning: looking inward at one's own mind
items.example: His diary is a record of quiet introspection.
items.exampleCN: 他的日记是一份安静内省的记录。

items.meaning: a printed plan that lets you look ahead
items.meaningCN: 章程；招股书（让人预先看清全貌）
items.example: The university's prospectus lists every course.
items.exampleCN: 这所大学的章程列出了每一门课程。

latinEntries.meaning: to look forward, look out on

definition_zh: 爱好者；恋人；情人；热爱者
definition_en: a person who loves someone romantically; also a person who greatly enjoys a particular activity or subject
core_image: 一个人把一束花轻轻放进另一双手里，目光只停在对方脸上
scene: 黄昏的街角，一个人把写好的信折好，塞进对方家的门缝，随后快步走开。 The lover waited by the fountain every evening, holding a small red box.
sceneCN: 这里 lover 是「恋人、情人」（第 2 个义项：恋爱对象）；句意为恋人每晚都等在喷泉边，手里拿着一个小红盒。画面里可认出街角、折好的信与喷泉。

pos.zh: 爱好者；恋人；情人；热爱者

derivatives.zh: 构成 lover 的名词基础，义为「爱；爱情」
由 love 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「可爱的；美好的」
由 love 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「惹人喜爱的」

senses.title: A person who greatly enjoys an activity or subject
senses.definition: a person who takes great interest and pleasure in a particular activity, subject or object
senses.definitionCN: 对某项活动、学科或事物有浓厚兴趣并从中获得乐趣的人
senses.example: She is a lifelong music lover who never misses a concert.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一辈子的音乐爱好者，从不错过任何一场音乐会。
senses.why: The verb love means to hold something dear, and the person suffix -er turns that feeling into an identity, so anyone who loves a thing deeply can be called its lover.
senses.whyCN: 动词 love 表示珍视某物，表示「人」的后缀 -er 把这种感情变成一种身份，所以任何深爱某事物的人都可以被称为它的 lover。

senses.title: A person someone is in a romantic relationship with
senses.definition: a person with whom someone has a romantic and usually sexual relationship
senses.definitionCN: 与某人处于恋爱关系、通常也包含性关系的人
senses.example: He wrote a letter to his lover before leaving the city.
senses.exampleCN: 离开这座城市之前，他给恋人写了一封信。
senses.why: Romantic love is the most intense form of holding someone dear, so the same person suffix naturally names the one who receives that love rather than the one who only feels it.
senses.whyCN: 恋爱是「珍视某人」最强烈的一种形式，于是同一个表示人的后缀自然指接受这份爱的那个人，而不只是付出爱的人。

senses.title: A person in a secret or extramarital sexual relationship
senses.definition: a person who has a sexual relationship with someone who is married to another person or already has a partner
senses.definitionCN: 与已婚者或已有伴侣者保持性关系的人；婚外情人
senses.example: The novel opens with a married man meeting his lover in a small hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 小说一开头，一个已婚男子在一家小旅馆与情人见面。
senses.why: Because the romantic sense is strong, the word takes on a discreet and often disapproving colour when the relationship has to be hidden from a spouse.
senses.whyCN: 因为恋爱义很强烈，当这种关系必须对配偶隐瞒时，这个词就带上隐秘、常含贬义的色彩，用来指婚外情人。

intro.en: Lover is love plus the person suffix -er; love itself goes back to an Old English word for deep affection.
intro.cn: lover 是 love 加表示「人」的后缀 -er；love 本身可追溯到古英语中表示深厚感情的词。

items.en: Old English lufu named love as a feeling, and the verb lufian meant to love or to hold dear.
items.cn: 古英语 lufu 指「爱」这种感情，动词 lufian 意为爱、珍视。

items.en: The reconstructed ancestor is lubō, a form rebuilt by comparing related Germanic languages rather than found in writing.
items.cn: 其重构祖形为 lubō，这一形式是通过比较相关日耳曼语言重建出来的，并非见于书面记录。

items.en: Middle English joined love with -er and produced lover, a person who loves or is loved.
items.cn: 中古英语把 love 与 -er 结合，造出 lover，指爱着别人或被爱的人。

items.en: The word covered both the devoted admirer of an art and the partner in a romance, and context decided which one was meant.
items.cn: 这个词同时指对某门艺术痴迷的爱好者和恋爱中的伴侣，具体指哪一个由上下文决定。

items.en: Modern English keeps the romantic sense at the centre, while compounds such as music lover and nature lover preserve the older sense of devoted admirer.
items.cn: 现代英语以恋爱义为中心，而 music lover、nature lover 这类复合词保留了「痴迷的爱好者」这一较早含义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the love family and its derived forms; the near-meaning group collects other words for people who love, admire or are loved.
note.cn: 形近组收 love 词族及其派生形式；近义组收其他表示爱慕、欣赏或被爱的人称。

entries.definition: A deep feeling of affection for a person or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 对人或事物怀有的深厚感情；爱。

entries.definition: Pleasing and attractive; built from love with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 讨人喜欢、好看的；由 love 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Easy to love because of a warm character.
entries.definitionCN: 因性格温暖而容易让人喜爱的。

entries.definition: Greatly loved, often used of a person who is dear to many.
entries.definitionCN: 深受爱戴的，常形容被众人珍视的人。

entries.definition: A person who likes, respects or loves someone, sometimes secretly.
entries.definitionCN: 喜欢、敬重或爱慕某人的人，有时是暗中的。

entries.definition: A person strongly devoted to a hobby, cause or person.
entries.definitionCN: 对某项爱好、事业或某人极为投入的人。

entries.definition: A person with eager and active interest in a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 对某一主题怀有热切而积极兴趣的人。

entries.definition: A person one loves romantically; an affectionate form of address.
entries.definitionCN: 所爱的恋人；也用作亲昵称呼。

normalIntro.en: The word is a transparent build from love and the person suffix -er, so its hooks come from the feeling, the suffix and the compounds it forms.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由 love 与表示人的后缀 -er 清楚构成，记忆钩子来自这份感情、这个后缀以及它组成的复合词。

normal.en: Lover is love plus -er, so the word literally means the one who loves.
normal.cn: lover 是 love 加 -er，字面意思就是「爱的那个人」。

normal.en: The plural is lovers, made by adding s to the singular.
normal.cn: 复数是 lovers，直接在单数后加 s。

normal.en: Music lover and nature lover are fixed compounds that keep the sense of devoted admirer.
normal.cn: music lover 与 nature lover 是固定复合词，保留了「痴迷的爱好者」这层意思。

normal.en: Beloved adds the prefix be- to loved, giving the sense of being greatly loved.
normal.cn: beloved 在 loved 前加前缀 be-，表示「深受爱戴的」。

normal.en: Lover names a person, while love names the feeling or the person addressed, so the two words split the roles.
normal.cn: lover 指人，love 指感情或对对方的称呼，两个词分担了不同角色。

abstract.en: A suffix that turns a feeling into a person shows how English builds identities out of emotions.
abstract.cn: 一个把感情变成人的后缀，说明英语会用情感来构造身份。

abstract.en: The same word can name a concert fan and a secret partner, because both are defined by what they love.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能指音乐会的粉丝，也能指秘密情人，因为两者都由「爱什么」来定义。

abstract.en: Lover reminds us that love is not only felt inside but always points at someone or something outside.
abstract.cn: lover 提醒人：爱不只是在心里感受，它总是指向外的某个人或某样东西。

examples.en: She is a lifelong music lover who never misses a concert.
examples.cn: 她是一辈子的音乐爱好者，从不错过任何一场音乐会。

examples.en: He wrote a letter to his lover before leaving the city.
examples.cn: 离开这座城市之前，他给恋人写了一封信。

examples.en: The garden was planted by two nature lovers who met at a birdwatching club.
examples.cn: 这座花园是两位在观鸟俱乐部相识的自然爱好者种下的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉我」——恋爱时总想拉住对方的手，记住 lover 是恋人。

root: love（古英语 lufu，爱）加表示「人」的后缀 -er；lufu 一般认为来自原始日耳曼语 lubō，属日耳曼语族词汇，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a person defined by love; the senses divide into the devoted admirer, the romantic partner and the hidden partner.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是由「爱」来定义的人；义项分出痴迷的爱好者、恋爱对象，以及隐秘的情人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person placing a bunch of flowers into another pair of hands, eyes fixed on the other face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人把一束花放进另一双手里，目光只停在对方脸上。

branches.en: a concert hall full of people who know every song
branches.cn: 坐满熟记每首歌的听众的音乐厅

branches.en: a gardener who names every bird that visits
branches.cn: 能叫出每只来访鸟名的园丁

branches.en: a letter folded and pushed under a door
branches.cn: 折好塞进门缝的信

branches.en: a quiet meeting in a small hotel
branches.cn: 小旅馆里的秘密会面

branches.en: a person whose love is both a hobby and a bond
branches.cn: 既是爱好又是羁绊的爱

intro.en: Lover is built from a Germanic noun of affection and an English person suffix, and the same root later forms adjectives and a prefixed participle.
intro.cn: lover 由日耳曼语中表示感情的名词与英语表示人的后缀构成，同一词根后来又造出形容词和带前缀的分词。

latinIntro.en: Love is a Germanic word, so lover has no reliable Latin cognate recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: love 是日耳曼语词，因此 lover 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.example: Old English lufu is the noun behind modern love.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 lufu 是 modern love 背后的名词。

items.example: Love can be quiet and steady rather than dramatic.
items.exampleCN: 爱可以安静而稳定，不必轰轰烈烈。

items.meaningCN: 后缀：做某事或怀有某种感情的人
items.example: A lover is the person who loves.
items.exampleCN: lover 就是爱着的那个人。

items.meaning: a person who loves or is devoted
items.example: The lover of old maps spent hours in the archive.
items.exampleCN: 这位旧地图爱好者泡在档案室好几个小时。

items.example: The two lovers met under the station clock.
items.exampleCN: 两个恋人在车站大钟下相会。

items.example: They spent a lovely afternoon by the river.
items.exampleCN: 他们在河边度过了一个美好的下午。

items.example: The dog was noisy but utterly lovable.
items.exampleCN: 这条狗很吵，却十分惹人喜爱。

items.example: The beloved teacher retired after forty years.
items.exampleCN: 这位深受爱戴的老师教了四十年后退休。

definition_zh: 盖子；眼睑；限制；压制
definition_en: a removable cover for a container; also the fold of skin over the eye, or a check placed on something
core_image: 一只手捏住锅盖的提钮，把热气和味道扣在锅里
scene: 厨房里热气腾腾，锅里的汤咕嘟作响。 She lifted the lid and let the steam escape.
sceneCN: 这里是「盖子」（第 1 个义项：容器的盖）；句意为她掀开锅盖，让蒸汽散出去。图中可辨识物件：汤锅、木质锅盖、灶火。

derivatives.zh: 由 eye 与 lid 复合而成，义为「眼皮；眼睑」
由 lid 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，义为「无盖的；没有眼皮的」
由 lid 加表示「具有」的后缀 -ed 构成，义为「带盖的」

senses.title: A cover for a container
senses.definition: a removable cover that fits over the top of a pot, box or other container
senses.definitionCN: 盖在锅、箱等容器顶部、可以取下的盖
senses.example: She lifted the lid of the pot and stirred the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 她掀开锅盖，搅了搅汤。
senses.why: The oldest sense names the thing that closes a container; Old English hlid meant a covering that keeps what is inside in place.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项指「把容器合上的东西」；古英语 hlid 就指覆盖物，作用是让里面的东西留在原处。

senses.title: Either fold of skin over the eye
senses.definition: one of the two movable folds of skin that close over the eye
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖在眼球上、可以开合的两片皮肤之一
senses.example: His lids grew heavy as the film went on.
senses.exampleCN: 电影越放越久，他的眼皮越发沉重。
senses.why: Closing the eye is covering it, so the same word for a cover was extended to the fold that covers the eyeball.
senses.whyCN: 合眼就是把眼睛盖上，于是原本表示覆盖物的词，被用来指遮住眼球的那层皮。

senses.title: A check or limit on something
senses.definition: a limit that keeps an activity, price or piece of news under control
senses.definitionCN: 把某项活动、价格或消息控制住的界限
senses.example: The mayor promised to keep a lid on city spending.
senses.exampleCN: 市长承诺要管住市里的开支。
senses.why: A lid seals a container, and in speech the image becomes a seal on spending or news, so the word names control rather than a physical cover.
senses.whyCN: 盖子能把容器封住；用到言语里，被封住的对象变成开支或消息，于是这个词表示「控住」，而不是实物盖子。

intro.en: Lid is an Old English word for a cover, and its eye and restraint senses grow out of the same act of closing something.
intro.cn: lid 是古英语里表示覆盖物的词，眼睑与「压制」两个义项都从「把东西合上」这个动作长出来。

items.en: A reconstructed noun for a covering is believed to stand behind the Old English word, though its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为古英语词背后有一个表示覆盖物的原始日耳曼语名词，但更深层的来源不确定。

items.en: Hlid named a cover for a container, and it could also name the covering of the eye.
items.cn: hlid 指容器的盖，也可以指眼睛上的那层覆盖。

items.en: Middle English kept lid for both the pot cover and the eyelid, and the spelling settled without the initial h.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lid 同时指锅盖与眼皮，拼写定型下来，词首的 h 不再写出。

items.en: The word spread from kitchens to workshops and became the ordinary noun for any removable cover.
items.cn: 这个词从厨房走进作坊，成为任何可取下盖子的常用名词。

items.en: Modern English adds a figurative restraint, so that a budget or a rumour can be sealed like a pot.
items.cn: 现代英语给它添上一层比喻性的「压制」，使预算或传闻也能像锅一样被封住。

note.en: The first group collects words built on the same cover image or close in spelling; the second collects other names for covers.
note.cn: 第一组收同一「覆盖」意象或拼写相近的词；第二组收其他表示覆盖物的词。

entries.definition: The fold of skin that covers the eye, built from eye and lid.
entries.definitionCN: 由 eye 与 lid 复合而成，指覆盖眼睛的那层皮，即眼皮。

entries.definition: Without a lid, or without eyelids.
entries.definitionCN: 没有盖子的，或没有眼皮的。

entries.definition: Having a lid, often of a stated kind.
entries.definitionCN: 带盖的，常用来说明盖子是什么样子。

entries.definition: The past tense of slide; it only resembles lid in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: slide 的过去式；只是拼写与 lid 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A thing placed over something to protect or close it.
entries.definitionCN: 盖在上面起保护或封闭作用的东西；盖子。

entries.definition: A small lid or top for a bottle or pen.
A plug that closes the mouth of a bottle or tube.
entries.definitionCN: 塞住瓶口或管口的塞子。

normalIntro.en: Lid is a short Old English word for a cover, and its family keeps the picture of something closing over an opening.
normalIntro.cn: lid 是古英语里表示覆盖物的短词，它的同族词都保留「把开口合上」的画面。

normal.en: Old English hlid meant a cover, and the h simply dropped away in Middle English.
normal.cn: 古英语 hlid 意为覆盖物，到了中古英语，词首的 h 就消失了。

normal.en: Eyelid is eye plus lid: the lid that covers the eye.
normal.cn: eyelid 是 eye 加 lid，即盖住眼睛的那片「盖子」。

normal.en: Lidless drops the cover, so it means having no lid or no eyelids.
normal.cn: lidless 去掉盖子，所以表示没有盖子或没有眼皮。

normal.en: Keep a lid on turns a kitchen cover into a limit on money, noise or news.
normal.cn: keep a lid on 把厨房的盖子变成对钱、声音或消息的限制。

normal.en: A pot lid and a dustbin lid differ only in what they seal, not in the shape of the word.
normal.cn: 锅盖与垃圾桶盖不同的只是封住什么，词形本身不变。

abstract.en: Anything that can be opened has a lid, which is why the word moves so easily from pots to eyes to budgets.
abstract.cn: 凡是可以打开的东西都有盖子，所以这个词能轻易从锅移到眼睛，再移到预算。

abstract.en: A lid does not hide what is inside; it keeps it from escaping, and that is the link between cover and control.
abstract.cn: 盖子并不隐藏里面的东西，而是不让它跑出来，这正是「覆盖」与「控制」之间的连接。

abstract.en: The word is short and shut like the thing it names, a small sound that closes a container.
abstract.cn: 这个词又短又闭合，像它所指的东西，一个短短的音就把容器合上。

examples.en: She lifted the lid of the pot and stirred the soup.
examples.cn: 她掀开锅盖，搅了搅汤。

examples.en: His lids felt heavy after the long drive.
examples.cn: 长途开车之后，他的眼皮沉得厉害。

examples.en: The coach kept a lid on the team's excitement before the final.
examples.cn: 决赛前，教练压住了队员们的兴奋情绪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离得」——盖子离得开，才装得下东西；lid 就是盖子。

root: 古英语 hlid（覆盖物、盖子）一般认为来自原始日耳曼语表示覆盖的名词，更深词源不确定；同族词多与「合上、遮住」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a cover that closes an opening; the senses spread to the cover of the eye and then to any limit that keeps something under control.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是合上开口的覆盖物；义项先扩展到眼睛上的覆盖，再扩展到把某事关住的限制。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand turning a lid shut on a steaming pot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把锅盖扣在冒着热气的锅上。

branches.en: steam trapped under a pot lid
branches.cn: 蒸汽被锅盖压住

branches.en: a blink that shuts the eye for a moment
branches.cn: 一次眨眼把眼睛短暂合上

branches.en: a child rubbing heavy lids at bedtime
branches.cn: 孩子睡前揉着发沉的眼皮

branches.en: a mayor capping the city budget
branches.cn: 市长给市政预算封顶

branches.en: reporters trying to lift the lid on a deal
branches.cn: 记者想揭开一桩交易的内情

intro.en: A short Germanic noun of covering, one English compound, and two endings that say what a thing has or lacks.
intro.cn: 一个表示覆盖的日耳曼短名词、一个英语复合词，以及两个说明「有」或「无」的词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for lid; Latin operculum also means a cover, but it belongs to another root.
latinIntro.cn: lid 没有可靠的拉丁同族词；拉丁语 operculum 也指盖子，但属于另一个词根。

items.meaning: the cover of a rubbish bin

definition_zh: 创造；创建；创作；创作物；产物
definition_en: the act of making something exist that did not exist before, or the thing that is made
core_image: 空白的画布上落下第一笔，一件原本不存在的东西出现了
scene: 美术馆的展厅里，人们围在一幅巨大的新画前低声赞叹，作者站在角落。 Everyone admired the young artist's latest creation.
sceneCN: 这里 creation 指「创作物」（第 3 个义项：被创作出来的具体作品）；句意是所有人都赞叹这位年轻画家最新的作品。

senses.title: The act of making something new
senses.definition: the act or process of making something exist that did not exist before
senses.definitionCN: 使原本不存在的东西得以存在的行为或过程
senses.example: The creation of new jobs helped the town recover.
senses.exampleCN: 新岗位的创造帮助这个镇子恢复了元气。
senses.why: The Latin stem creare means to bring forth, so the noun first names the act of bringing forth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干 creare 意为「使生出」，所以名词首先指「使生出」这一行为本身。

senses.title: The act of inventing or designing
senses.definition: the act of producing a work of art, writing, or design using imagination
senses.definitionCN: 凭想象力产出艺术、文字或设计作品的行为
senses.example: The creation of the character took the author ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个人物的创作花了作者十年时间。
senses.why: When what is brought forth is imagined rather than manufactured, the word narrows to artistic making.
senses.whyCN: 当「生出」的东西来自想象而非制造时，这个词收窄为艺术创作。

senses.title: A thing that has been made
senses.definition: something that someone has made or invented, especially something unusual or imaginative
senses.definitionCN: 某人造出或发明的东西，尤指独特或富有想象力之物
senses.example: The garden is his most unusual creation.
senses.exampleCN: 这座花园是他最不寻常的创作。
senses.why: A finished act of making leaves behind an object, so the noun also names the object itself.
senses.whyCN: 完成的创造会留下一个对象，于是名词也转指这个被造出来的东西。

senses.title: The making of the world
senses.definition: the making of the world and everything in it, especially in religious belief
senses.definitionCN: 世界及其中万物的被造，尤见于宗教信仰
senses.example: The story describes the creation of the world in seven days.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事讲述了世界在七日内被造的过程。
senses.why: Only a supreme maker can bring the whole world forth, so the word rises to the cosmic scale.
senses.whyCN: 能把整个世界生出来的唯有至高造物者，于是这个词升格到宇宙尺度。

senses.title: The whole world of living things
senses.definition: all the living things in the world, thought of together
senses.definitionCN: 把世上一切生灵合起来看的整体
senses.example: All creation seemed to fall silent before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨来临前，天地众生仿佛都安静了下来。
senses.why: Every living thing is a made thing, so the made world as a whole can be called creation.
senses.whyCN: 每个生灵都是被造之物，于是被造的世界整体也可以称为「万物」。

intro.en: Creation comes from Latin creare, to make or bring forth, through creatio, the act of making.
intro.cn: creation 源自拉丁语 creare（创造、生出），经 creatio（创造行为）进入英语。

items.en: The root *ker- is generally reconstructed as meaning to grow or make grow.
items.cn: 词根 *ker- 一般被重构为「生长、使生长」之义。

items.en: Creare meant to make something come forth or grow; creatio named the act of making.
items.cn: creare 意为使某物生出或生长；creatio 指创造这一行为。

items.en: Creacion carried the same religious and general sense of making.
items.cn: creacion 带有同样泛指与宗教意义上的「创造」义。

items.en: Creation first appeared in English chiefly for the making of the world by God.
items.cn: creation 初入英语时主要指上天创造世界。

items.en: It widened to any act of making and to the thing made, including works of art.
items.cn: 它扩展为任何创造行为及其产物，包括艺术作品。

items.en: It now covers founding things, inventing designs, and naming the results.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖创建事物、设计发明，并指创造出来的成果。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the creat- stem, and the near-meaning group names other acts or results of making.
note.cn: 形近组共享 creat- 词干，近义组列出其他表示创造行为或成果的说法。

entries.definition: to make something new exist
good at making new and original things
entries.definitionCN: 善于造出新颖原创之物的

entries.definition: a person or force that makes something
a new device or idea that someone has thought up
entries.definitionCN: 想出来的新装置或新点子

entries.definition: a piece of art, music, or writing
entries.definitionCN: 一件艺术、音乐或文字作品

entries.definition: a work of art made with great skill
entries.definitionCN: 以高超技艺完成的艺术作品

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from the first stroke on a blank canvas to the finished thing hanging on the wall.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从空白画布上的第一笔，一直走到挂在墙上的成品。

normal.en: Create plus -ion: the act of creating, then the thing created.
normal.cn: create 加 -ion：先指创造这一行为，再指被造出来的东西。

normal.en: Creation = creation of jobs, creation of art, creation of the world.
normal.cn: creation 的三大常用面：创造岗位、艺术创作、创世。

normal.en: Every creation needs a creator.
normal.cn: 每件创作物背后都有一个创造者。

normal.en: The -ion ending turns the verb into a noun you can count.
normal.cn: -ion 后缀把动词变成可数的名词。

normal.en: Creation and creative share the same first letters and the same family.
normal.cn: creation 与 creative 同头同族，一起记。

abstract.en: Picture the first brushstroke on a blank canvas.
abstract.cn: 想象空白画布上落下的第一笔。

abstract.en: Picture a lump of clay slowly becoming a figure.
abstract.cn: 想象一团黏土慢慢变成一个人像。

abstract.en: Picture a newborn star lighting an empty sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗新星照亮空无一物的天空。

examples.en: The creation of the park took only two years.
examples.cn: 这座公园的建成只花了两年。

examples.en: Her latest creation won first prize at the fair.
examples.cn: 她的最新作品在展会上得了头奖。

examples.en: They discussed stories about the creation of the world.
examples.cn: 他们讨论了关于创世的种种故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 creation 记成 create（创造）加 -ion：创造这一行为是创造，创造出来的东西也是创作，一横一竖正好两个方向。

root: 源自拉丁语 creare（创造、生出），名词形式 creatio 指「创造行为」，经古法语 creacion 于十四世纪进入英语；本义是「使某物生出」，先专指上天创世，后扩展到一切创造行为及其产物。

sensesIntro.en: From the bare act of making something exist, creation widens to artistic invention, then to the thing made, and finally to the making of the world itself.
sensesIntro.cn: creation 从「使某物存在」的赤裸行为出发，扩展到艺术创作，再转指创作物，最终上升到创世与天地众生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first stroke on a blank canvas — something now exists that did not exist before
core.cn: 核心意象：空白画布上的第一笔——原本不存在的东西从此存在了

branches.en: Bringing jobs, systems, or organizations into existence.
branches.cn: 使岗位、体系或组织从无到有。

branches.en: Imagining and designing a work of art or writing.
branches.cn: 凭想象设计与产出艺术或文字作品。

branches.en: The finished object that the act of making leaves behind.
branches.cn: 创造行为留下的成品本身。

branches.en: The religious account of the world being made.
branches.cn: 宗教中世界被造的叙事。

branches.en: All living things viewed as one made world.
branches.cn: 把一切生灵看作同一个被造的世界。

intro.en: Creation is built from a Latin verb stem plus a noun suffix; the same family shares one stem.
intro.cn: creation 由拉丁动词词干加名词后缀构成；同族词共享同一个词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem goes back to Latin creare, and the suffix -ion goes back to Latin -io, which turns verbs into nouns of action.
latinIntro.cn: 词干可追溯到拉丁语 creare，后缀 -ion 源自拉丁语 -io，用于把动词变成表行为的名词。

items.example: create means to make something new
items.exampleCN: create 意为造出新的东西

items.example: action means the act of doing
items.exampleCN: action 意为做这件事的行为

items.example: creativity means the quality of being creative

definition_zh: 对手；竞争者；与…匹敌；竞争的
definition_en: a person or group competing for the same thing, or to match them
core_image: 同一条街上争抢客人的两家小店
scene: 同一条街上的两家店铺互相竞争，争抢同一批客人。 The two shops on the same street are rivals for the same customers.
sceneCN: 这里 rival 是「对手」（第 1 个义项：争夺同一目标的竞争者）；句意：同一条街上的两家店铺互相竞争，争抢同一批客人。

senses.title: One who competes
senses.definition: a person or group trying to win the same thing
senses.definitionCN: 试图赢得同一目标的人或群体
senses.example: Her main rival trains in the same gym.
senses.exampleCN: 她的主要对手在同一家健身房训练。
senses.why: Two people sharing one stream must compete for it.
senses.whyCN: 共用一条溪流的人必然要争夺它。

senses.title: To match someone
senses.definition: to be as good as someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 与某人或某物一样出色
senses.example: No one can rival her skill at chess.
senses.exampleCN: 没人能在棋艺上与她匹敌。
senses.why: A worthy opponent raises the level of both.
senses.whyCN: 强劲的对手会把双方的水平都抬高。

senses.title: Competing
senses.definition: competing for the same market or aim
senses.definitionCN: 争夺同一市场或目标的
senses.example: The rival firm cut its prices.
senses.exampleCN: 竞争对手公司降低了价格。
senses.why: The adjective marks the other side of the race.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记竞赛的另一方。

intro.en: Rival comes from Latin rivalis, one who uses the same stream, from rivus, a stream.
intro.cn: rival 源自拉丁语 rivalis，意为共用同一条溪流的人，来自 rivus（溪流）。

items.en: Rivus means a stream.
items.cn: rivus 意为溪流。

items.en: Rivalis is one who shares the stream.
items.cn: rivalis 指共用溪流的人。

items.en: French rival keeps the sense of a competitor.
items.cn: 法语 rival 保留了竞争者的含义。

items.en: English rival names a rival in love or sport.
items.cn: 英语 rival 指情感或竞技中的对手。

items.en: Business gives the word its widest use.
items.cn: 商业让这个词使用最广。

note.en: A rival is close enough to compete; an enemy wishes to harm.
note.cn: rival 是实力相当、彼此竞争的对手，enemy 是想伤害对方的人。

entries.definition: competition between rivals
more than one rival
matching or competing
a person or firm competing
the other side in a contest
one who challenges a leader

normalIntro.en: Rivals once shared one stream and fought over it.
normalIntro.cn: rival 原本指共用一条溪流并为之争夺的人。

normal.en: A rival company wants your customers.
normal.cn: rival company 想要你的顾客。

normal.en: A business rival is a firm you compete with.
normal.cn: business rival 是与你在生意上竞争的公司。

normal.en: A rival team stands on the other side.
normal.cn: rival team 站在赛场的另一边。

normal.en: An arch rival is your biggest opponent.
normal.cn: arch rival 是你最大的对手。

normal.en: Rivalry is the noun for the fight between them.
normal.cn: rivalry 是双方对抗的名词。

abstract.en: Picture two farmers at one narrow ditch.
abstract.cn: 想象两个农夫在一条窄渠两端。

abstract.en: Imagine two runners shoulder to shoulder.
abstract.cn: 想象两名跑者肩并着肩。

abstract.en: Think of two shop signs facing each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两块店招面对面挂起。

examples.en: The two cities are rivals for the trade.
examples.cn: 这两座城市是贸易上的竞争对手。

examples.en: Nobody could rival his patience.
examples.cn: 没有人能比得上他的耐心。

examples.en: A rival seller opened next door.
examples.cn: 一位竞争卖家在隔壁开了店。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rival」听起来像「来否」——总来争抢同一个目标的，就是对手。

root: 拉丁语 rivus（溪流）→ rivalis（共用溪流者）→ rival，核心义「争夺同一资源、实力相当的对手」。

sensesIntro.en: A rival competes for the same goal, can match another's ability, or acts as a competing force.
sensesIntro.cn: rival 指争夺同一目标的对手，也可指与某人匹敌，或作形容词表示竞争的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people at one narrow stream.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人在一条窄溪旁。

branches.en: The competitor is the main noun sense.
branches.cn: 竞争者是最主要的名词义项。

branches.en: To match a rival is to reach their level.
branches.cn: 与对手匹敌就是达到他们的水平。

branches.en: The adjective marks the opposite side.
branches.cn: 形容词标记对立的一方。

branches.en: Real rivals make each other stronger.
branches.cn: 真正的对手让彼此更强。

branches.en: The noun and adjective both name the other side.
branches.cn: 名词与形容词都指另一方。

intro.en: Rival comes from Latin rivus, a stream.
intro.cn: rival 来自拉丁语 rivus（溪流）。

latinIntro.en: Rivalis, one who shares a stream, gives the French and English word.
latinIntro.cn: rivalis（共用溪流的人）给出了法语和英语中的这个词。

latinEntries.example: Rivus explains why rivals share water.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rivus 解释了对手为何共享水源。

latinEntries.example: Rivalis is the source of rival.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rivalis 是 rival 的来源。

definition_zh: 山谷；河谷；流域；凹处
definition_en: a low stretch of land between hills, often with a river running through it
core_image: 两侧山坡倾斜下来，中间一条河慢慢流过
scene: 清晨的雾还没散，两侧山脊像两道墙，河在底部弯了一下，把村子圈在里面。 The village sits in a narrow valley below the pass.
sceneCN: 这里 valley 是「山谷」（第 1 个义项：山间的低地）；句意为村子坐落在山口下方一道狭窄的山谷里。两侧山坡夹着一条河的画面，正是这个词的核心。

collocations.phrase: valley of the shadow of death

derivatives.zh: 同源名词，义为「谷；（诗）山谷」

senses.title: Low land between hills
senses.definition: a long low area of land lying between hills or mountains
senses.definitionCN: 夹在山丘或高山之间的一片狭长低地
senses.example: A small stream runs along the bottom of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 一条小溪沿着谷底流过。
senses.why: Latin vallis named the fold itself, and the landform is the plainest thing the word can point at.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vallis 指的就是这道褶皱，而地形正是这个词最初所指的东西。

senses.title: The land drained by a river
senses.definition: the area of land through which a river runs and which it drains
senses.definitionCN: 一条河流经并汇集来水的整片土地
senses.example: The farms in the valley all depend on that one river.
senses.exampleCN: 河谷里的农场都靠这一条河。
senses.why: Water collects in the lowest line of the fold, so the river and the land it feeds take the same name.
senses.whyCN: 水总是汇聚到褶皱最低的那一线，于是河流与它养活的土地共用了这个名字。

senses.title: A dip or hollow in a surface
senses.definition: a low part in a line on a graph or in a surface
senses.definitionCN: 图表曲线或表面上的低洼部分
senses.example: Sales fell into a valley between two peaks.
senses.exampleCN: 销量在两个高峰之间落进了谷底。
senses.why: Any line that drops and rises again traces the same v shape, so the landform becomes a metaphor for a dip.
senses.whyCN: 任何先下后上的曲线都画出同一个 v 形，地形于是被借来比喻凹陷。

senses.title: A place that seems low or humble
senses.definition: in figurative use, a low point of fortune or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 引申指境遇或情绪的低点
senses.example: The years after the factory closed were a valley for the town.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关闭后的那些年是这个镇子的低谷。
senses.why: A low stretch between two highs of life is felt as a valley, and the picture of the landscape carries the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 人生两个高点之间那段低处被感受为谷，正是地形画面承载了这种情绪。

intro.en: A Latin word for a fold in the land, carried through French with the native twin dale beside it.
intro.cn: 一个指「大地褶皱」的拉丁词，经法语进入英语，旁边还站着本土兄弟词 dale。

items.en: Vallis or valles named a valley in classical Latin.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语用 vallis 或 valles 指山谷。

items.en: French made valee from the Latin stem, keeping the same shape of land.
items.cn: 法语从拉丁词干造出 valee，指的还是同样的地形。

items.en: Middle English borrows valee and spells it valley by the end of the period.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 valee，到该时期末拼作 valley。

items.en: The native word dale, from Old English dæl, already named the same thing.
items.cn: 本土词 dale 出自古英语 dæl，原本就指同一地形。

items.en: The sense widens to river basins, dips in graphs, and low points of fortune.
items.cn: 词义扩展到河流盆地、图表凹陷与境遇的低点。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the Latin and native words for the same landform, and the near-meaning group sets the low ground against its opposites.
note.cn: 形近组收集同指这一地形的拉丁词与本土词，近义组把低地与它的反面放在一起。

entries.definition: a valley, now chiefly poetic or in place names
entries.definitionCN: 山谷；现多用于诗歌或地名

entries.definition: the Latin noun for a valley
a valley, chiefly in northern English place names
entries.definitionCN: 山谷；多用于英格兰北部地名

entries.definition: a small valley with trees
a narrow steep-sided valley
a deep valley with steep rock sides
a wide low area drained by a river
a long narrow high top of land

normalIntro.en: Picture the shape of the letter v: two sides dropping to a floor, which is what a valley is.
normalIntro.cn: 想象字母 v 的形状：两侧向下收到一个底部，山谷正是如此。

normal.en: The plural is valleys, y kept before the s.
normal.cn: 复数是 valleys，y 后直接加 s。

normal.en: Valley floor is the standard phrase for the flat bottom.
normal.cn: 谷底的标准说法是 valley floor。

normal.en: Silicon Valley is a place name that now names an industry.
normal.cn: Silicon Valley 本是地名，现在也指一个产业。

normal.en: The old poetic form vale survives in place names.
normal.cn: 古老的诗歌形式 vale 仍留在地名中。

normal.en: Dale and dell are the native English cousins of valley.
normal.cn: dale 与 dell 是 valley 的英语本土兄弟词。

abstract.en: Picture mist sitting between two long ridges at dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时雾停在两道长山脊之间。

abstract.en: Follow a river bending once and enclosing a village.
abstract.cn: 顺着一条河打了个弯，把村子圈在里面。

abstract.en: See a sales chart dip into a u shape.
abstract.cn: 看销量曲线凹成一个 u 形。

examples.en: The road follows the valley for twenty kilometres.
examples.cn: 这条路沿着山谷延伸二十公里。

examples.en: Fog filled the valley floor before sunrise.
examples.cn: 日出前雾布满谷底。

examples.en: Many orchards in the valley were damaged by frost.
examples.cn: 山谷里的许多果园被霜冻毁了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「洼里」——地势往洼里陷下去的那一块，就是山谷。

root: 拉丁语 vallis（山谷），经古法语 valee 进入英语，拼作 valley

sensesIntro.en: A fold in the land gives the river that fills it, then any dip in a line or graph, and finally a low point of fortune.
sensesIntro.cn: 大地上的一道褶皱给出填满它的河流，再给出曲线或图表上的凹陷，最后给出境遇上的低谷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hillsides sloping down to a river.
core.cn: 核心意象：两侧山坡斜下，中间一条河。

branches.en: The landform branch: the plainest shape of the word.
branches.cn: 地形分支：这个词最朴素的形状。

branches.en: The river branch: water gathers in the fold.
branches.cn: 河流分支：水往褶皱里汇。

branches.en: The graph branch: any line that dips.
branches.cn: 图表分支：任何向下凹陷的曲线。

branches.en: The fortune branch: lows of emotion and of money.
branches.cn: 境遇分支：情绪与银钱上的低谷。

branches.en: The place-name branch: a district known as the valley.
branches.cn: 地名分支：整个区域被称作山谷。

intro.en: A Latin word for a fold in the land, reshaped by French, with dale and dell as its native partners.
intro.cn: 一个指大地褶皱的拉丁词，经法语改写而成，本土对应词是 dale 与 dell。

latinIntro.en: Latin vallis, valley, became valee in French and valley in English; the shortened vale is kept for poetry and names.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vallis（山谷）在法语中成 valee，在英语中成 valley；缩短的 vale 留给诗歌与地名。

items.example: The root vall- means a hollow between hills.
items.exampleCN: 词根 vall- 指山间低处。

items.example: The ending marks a stretch of land.
Dale is the Germanic partner word.
items.exampleCN: dale 是日耳曼语的对应词。

items.example: A dell is small and wooded.
A river valley is cut by water.

definition_zh: 表明；显示；指出；暗示
definition_en: to show that something exists or is likely, or to point it out
core_image: 手指在图纸上轻轻一点，示意某项出了问题
scene: 仪表盘上亮起红灯，说明发动机可能过热。 The gauge indicates a sudden rise in temperature.
sceneCN: 这里 indicate 是「显示」（第 1 个义项：表明某种情况存在）；句意是仪表显示温度突然升高。

pos.zh: 动词：表明；显示；指出；暗示

derivatives.zh: 义为「迹象、指示」，由本词加 -ion 构成
义为「表明的、暗示的」，常与 of 连用
义为「索引、指标」，与本词同根

senses.title: To show as a sign
senses.titleCN: 表明：作为某种情况的标志
senses.definition: to show that a state or event exists
senses.definitionCN: 显示出某种状况或事件存在
senses.example: The gauge indicates a sudden rise in temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 仪表显示温度突然升高。
senses.why: The Latin dicare means to make known, and in- points the gesture at something specific.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dicare 意为「使之知晓」，in- 则把这个动作指向具体对象。

senses.title: To point out directly
senses.definition: to show a thing to someone by pointing or naming it
senses.definitionCN: 通过指点或说出名称来把某物显示给人
senses.example: He indicated the seat beside him.
senses.exampleCN: 他指了指身边的座位。
senses.why: The oldest sense is physical: a finger makes the message known without words.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是具体的：一根手指不动嘴就把信息告知了。

senses.title: To suggest without saying
senses.definition: to make a wish or opinion known indirectly
senses.definitionCN: 间接地表露愿望或看法
senses.example: She indicated that she would rather stay.
senses.exampleCN: 她暗示自己宁可留下。
senses.why: A point can be polite as well as clear: the finger moves, the sentence remains unsaid.
senses.whyCN: 一指既可清晰也可含蓄：手指动了，话却没说出口。

senses.title: To be a sign of, of data
senses.titleCN: 表明：数据与研究中的用法
senses.definition: used of facts or studies to show what they suggest
senses.definitionCN: 用于事实或研究，表示其暗示的结论
senses.example: The results indicate that the method works.
senses.exampleCN: 结果表明这个方法有效。
senses.why: Research cannot speak, so the verb lets numbers point at a conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 研究本身不会说话，这个动词让数字指向一个结论。

senses.title: To signal on a vehicle
senses.titleCN: 打转向灯：车辆上的指示
senses.definition: to signal an intention to turn, using lights on a car
senses.definitionCN: 用汽车灯示意即将转向
senses.example: Always indicate before you turn.
senses.exampleCN: 转弯前一定要打转向灯。
senses.why: A machine repeats the gesture for you, so the word replaces the verb signal in British usage.
senses.whyCN: 机器代替人做这个手势，于是英式英语用这个词代替 signal。

intro.en: Indicate comes from Latin indicare, to point out, from in- and dicare, to make known.
intro.cn: indicate 来自拉丁语 indicare「指出」，由 in- 与 dicare「使之知晓」构成。

items.en: Dicare meant to proclaim or dedicate, from the same family as dicere, to say.
items.cn: dicare 意为宣告或奉献，与 dicere「说」同族。

items.en: Indicare meant to point out or show, often with a gesture.
items.cn: indicare 意为指出或显示，常伴手势。

items.en: English borrowed it to describe signs and measurements.
items.cn: 英语借它描述标志与测量结果。

items.en: The verb became a standard word in reports of data.
items.cn: 这个词成为报告数据时的标准用词。

items.en: British English made it the everyday word for signalling in a car.
items.cn: 英式英语让它成为汽车打转向灯的日常说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the indic- root; the near-meaning group holds verbs of showing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 indic- 词根；近义组收表示「显示」的动词。

entries.definition: A sign that something exists.
A gauge or sign that shows a level.
To give time or effort to a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「奉献」，与 indicate 形近。

entries.definition: To make something visible or clear.
To make someone think something is likely.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「暗示、表明」，语气更弱。

entries.definition: To make known something hidden.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「揭示」，强调原本隐藏。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the pointing gesture, the dictionary root and the turn signal.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借指点的手势、dictionary 词根与转向灯。

normal.en: Dictionary and dictate share the root to say; indicate is the root plus in, saying towards a thing.
normal.cn: dictionary 与 dictate 共有「说」的词根；indicate 就是该词根加 in，朝着某物说话。

normal.en: Indicate that is the standard opening of any scientific finding.
normal.cn: indicate that 是一切科学结论的标准开头。

normal.en: Indicate the seat: a finger does the work of a whole sentence.
normal.cn: indicate the seat：一根手指干完了一整句话的活。

normal.en: In British cars, indicate is written on the turn signal lever's job description.
normal.cn: 在英国车里，转向灯杆的职责就用 indicate 来写。

normal.en: Indication, indicator, indicative: the ending changes but the pointing stays.
normal.cn: indication、indicator、indicative：词尾在变，指点的动作不变。

abstract.en: To indicate is to stay one step short of proof, and careful writers keep that step.
abstract.cn: 表明离证明还差一步，谨慎的写作者会守住这一步。

abstract.en: A sign is always smaller than the thing it points to.
abstract.cn: 标志永远比它所指向的东西小。

abstract.en: Language indicates before it states, and most arguments turn on that gap.
abstract.cn: 语言先暗示再陈述，多数争论就出在这道缝隙上。

examples.en: The map indicates where the river bends.
examples.cn: 地图标出了河流拐弯的地方。

examples.en: Early studies indicated a strong link.
examples.cn: 早期研究显示出很强的关联。

examples.en: He indicated with a nod that he agreed.
examples.cn: 他点头表示同意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印地开的」——地图印得清楚，标示该走的方向。

root: 拉丁语 in-（朝向）+ dicare（使之知晓，源自 dicere「说」）→ indicare（指出）；同根词有 index、indication、dedicate、dictate、dictionary。

sensesIntro.en: Indicate begins as a finger making a thing known, then covers any sign, indirect hints, research findings and finally a car's signal lamp.
sensesIntro.cn: indicate 起于手指把某物点明，随后涵盖任何标志、间接暗示、研究结论，最后还指汽车上的信号灯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger tapping a blueprint to show where the fault lies.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指在图纸上轻点，示出故障所在。

branches.en: SIGN LINE: readings and results point at a condition.
branches.cn: 标志线：读数与结果指向某种状况。

branches.en: GESTURE LINE: a hand shows the object itself.
branches.cn: 手势线：手直接示出对象。

branches.en: POLITENESS LINE: a wish is expressed without words.
branches.cn: 委婉线：愿望不必说出口。

branches.en: DATA LINE: numbers point at a conclusion.
branches.cn: 数据线：数字指向一个结论。

branches.en: MACHINE LINE: a lamp repeats the gesture for the driver.
branches.cn: 机器线：一盏灯替司机重复这个手势。

intro.en: A Latin prefix for pointing at, a root for making known, and a verb ending.
intro.cn: 一个表示「指向」的拉丁前缀、一个意为「使之知晓」的词根，以及一个动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin in-, upon, plus dicare, to make known, plus -are gave indicare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in-「朝向」加 dicare「使之知晓」加 -are，构成 indicare。

definition_zh: 洗澡；浴缸；沐浴
definition_en: the act of washing the body in water, or the tub you sit in
core_image: 浴室里一只装满热水的白瓷浴缸
scene: 水汽把镜子蒙住了。 She took a warm bath after the long walk.
sceneCN: 这里 bath 是「洗澡」（第 1 个义项：在水中洗净身体的行为）；句意是长途步行后她洗了个热水澡。

derivatives.zh: 由 bath 与 room 构成，义为「浴室」
由 bath 与 tub 构成，义为「浴缸」

senses.title: Washing in water
senses.definition: the act of washing the whole body in water
senses.definitionCN: 在水中洗净全身的行为
senses.example: She took a warm bath after the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 长途步行后她洗了个热水澡。
senses.why: Bath comes from Old English baeth, which named both the water and the act of washing in it.
senses.whyCN: bath 来自古英语 baeth，兼指洗澡水与在水中洗浴的行为。

senses.title: The tub
senses.definition: a large container that you fill with water and sit in
senses.definitionCN: 注满水后可以坐进去的大容器
senses.example: The bath was full of hot water.
senses.exampleCN: 浴缸里放满了热水。
senses.why: The container and the act shared one name, so the tub itself can be called a bath.
senses.whyCN: 容器与行为共用一个名称，所以浴缸本身也叫 bath。

intro.en: Bath is an old English word for washing in water.
intro.cn: bath 是古英语中表示「在水中洗浴」的词。

items.cn: baeth 意为「沐浴」。

items.en: bath kept the sense of washing.

items.cn: bath 与 bathe 分化为名词与动词。

items.en: take a bath is the common phrase.
items.cn: 如今 take a bath 是常见搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group differs in the final sound; the near-meaning group gives washing words.
note.cn: 形近组在尾音上不同；近义组是洗浴相关的说法。

normalIntro.cn: bath 既是洗澡，也是你坐进去的浴缸。

abstract.en: See steam clouding a mirror.

abstract.en: See a white tub full of hot water.

abstract.en: See foam sliding down a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象泡沫顺着墙面滑下。

examples.en: She took a warm bath after the long walk.
examples.cn: 长途步行后她洗了个热水澡。

examples.en: The bath was full of hot water.
examples.cn: 浴缸里放满了热水。

examples.en: He ran a bath and left the door open.

dict_mnemonic.text: bath 有热气：热水一放，澡就洗上了。

root: 源自古英语 baeth「沐浴」，兼指洗澡水与洗浴行为；后也指盛水的浴缸，并与动词 bathe 分工。

sensesIntro.en: The act of washing and the vessel that holds the water share one old name.
sensesIntro.cn: 洗浴的行为与盛水的容器，共用一个古老的名称。
