definition_zh: 使确信；说服
definition_en: to make someone believe that something is true, or to persuade someone to act
core_image: 一个人把一条清楚的路指给另一个人看，对方终于点头
scene: 她拿出一张张照片，父亲看完后不再反对。 The photos convinced him that the plan was safe.
sceneCN: 这里 convince 指「使确信」（第 1 个义项：让某人相信某事为真）；句意是这些照片使他确信这个计划是安全的。

derivatives.zh: 有说服力的；令人信服的

senses.title: To make someone sure
senses.definition: to cause someone to believe that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 使某人相信某事为真
senses.example: The evidence convinced her that he was honest.
senses.exampleCN: 证据使她确信他是诚实的。
senses.why: Doubt is a door held shut, and proof is the hand that opens it.
senses.whyCN: 怀疑是一扇关着的门，证据就是推开它的那只手。

senses.title: To persuade into action
senses.definition: to talk someone into doing something
senses.definitionCN: 通过劝说使某人去做某事
senses.example: He convinced his parents to let him travel.
senses.exampleCN: 他说服父母让他去旅行。
senses.why: Belief is half the work; the other half is a step taken.
senses.whyCN: 相信只算一半，另一半是迈出那一步。

intro.en: Convince comes from Latin convincere, to overcome with proof, built from com-, together, and vincere, to conquer.
intro.cn: convince 来自拉丁语 convincere（用证据驳倒），由 com-（一起、完全）与 vincere（征服）构成。

items.en: Vincere meant to conquer an opponent in a struggle.
items.cn: vincere 意为在较量中战胜对手。

items.en: Convincere meant to defeat someone with reasons rather than force.
items.cn: convincere 意为用道理而非武力把人驳倒。

items.en: English convince first meant to prove a person wrong.
items.cn: 英语 convince 最初指证明某人有错。

items.en: The meaning softened to making someone feel certain.
items.cn: 词义变柔和，转为使某人感到确定。

items.en: A new pattern, convince someone to do, became common.
items.cn: convince someone to do 这一新搭配变得常见。

items.en: Today it covers both belief and action.
items.cn: 今天它同时涵盖相信与行动。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin conquering base vinc-, and the meaning group names other ways of bringing someone to a view.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的征服词基 vinc-，近义组列出其他使人接受看法的说法。

entries.definition: to find someone guilty in court
entries.definitionCN: 在法庭上判定某人有罪

entries.definition: able to make people believe
too strong to be beaten
to make someone agree to do something
to tell someone firmly so doubt goes away
entries.definitionCN: 坚定地告诉某人以消除疑虑

entries.definition: to give someone enough reason to accept
entries.definitionCN: 给某人足够的理由接受

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with proof winning a mind, then move to a person moving from doubt to a decision.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从证据赢下一个头脑开始，再到一个人从怀疑走向决定。

normal.en: Con- is completely and vince is to conquer, so convince is to conquer doubt completely.
normal.cn: con- 是完全，vince 是征服，convince 就是把怀疑彻底征服。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with convict: one changes a mind, the other closes a door.
normal.cn: 别和 convict 搞混：一个改变想法，一个关上牢门。

normal.en: You convince a friend; you convict a defendant.
normal.cn: 你说服朋友；你给被告定罪。

normal.en: The adjective convincing adds -ing, as if the argument is still working on you.
normal.cn: 形容词 convincing 加了 -ing，仿佛那套论证还在你身上起作用。

normal.en: A convinced person walks differently from a merely informed one.
normal.cn: 确信的人走路的姿态，和仅仅被告知的人不一样。

abstract.en: Picture a locked gate opening after a key turns.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙转动后，锁着的门开了。

abstract.en: Picture a scale slowly settling on one side.
abstract.cn: 想象天平慢慢落向一边。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing down a clear road at dusk.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏里一只手指出一条清楚的路。

examples.en: Nothing you say will convince me otherwise.
examples.cn: 你说什么也无法使我相信别的。

examples.en: She convinced the class to join the clean-up.
examples.cn: 她说服全班参加清洁活动。

examples.en: His explanation was simple and convincing.
examples.cn: 他的解释简单而有说服力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 convince 记成 con（完全）加 vince（征服）：把对方的怀疑完全征服，就是使确信、说服。

root: 源自拉丁语 convincere（用证据驳倒），由 com-（完全）与 vincere（征服）构成，本指以理服人，后指使确信与说服。

sensesIntro.en: From proof winning a mind, to a mind deciding to move.
sensesIntro.cn: 从证据赢下一个头脑，到这个头脑决定行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pointing down a clear road.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手指出一条清楚的路。

branches.en: Evidence settles the question of what is true.
branches.cn: 证据解决了什么为真这个问题。

branches.en: A settled mind then agrees to act.
branches.cn: 安定的心随后同意行动。

branches.en: Belief and action are two halves of one movement.
branches.cn: 相信与行动是同一个动作的两半。

branches.en: The first sense is about truth and evidence.
branches.cn: 第一个义项关乎真相与证据。

branches.en: The second is about will and permission.
branches.cn: 第二个义项关乎意愿与许可。

intro.en: Convince is built on Latin com-, completely, plus vincere, to conquer.
intro.cn: convince 由拉丁语 com-（完全）与 vincere（征服）构成。

latinIntro.en: The conquering base vinc- also runs through convict, victory and invincible.
latinIntro.cn: 征服词基 vinc- 也贯穿 convict、victory 与 invincible。

items.exampleCN: 随后是一场令人信服的胜利。

items.meaning: the gaining of the upper hand

items.exampleCN: 他们觉得自己不可战胜。

items.meaning: to put a person out by force

definition_zh: 出现；浮现；显露；脱颖而出
definition_en: to come out from a hidden place; to become known; to come into existence; to survive a difficult period
core_image: 水面下的一团影子慢慢升起，终于露出水面
scene: 云层裂开，太阳从背后露出边缘。 The sun emerged from behind the clouds.
sceneCN: 这里 emerge 是「露出、出现」（第 01 个义项：从遮蔽处出来）；句意是太阳从云层后露出。

pos.zh: 不及物动词：出现；浮现；显露；脱颖而出

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ence 构成，义为「出现；兴起」
由动词加 -ent 构成，义为「新兴的；浮现的」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「新兴的；正在出现的」

senses.title: To come out from a hidden place
senses.definition: to move out of water, darkness or another covering and become visible
senses.definitionCN: 从水中、暗处或其他遮盖物里出来并变得可见
senses.example: The sun emerged from behind the clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳从云层后露出。
senses.why: The Latin verb joins e-, out, with mergere, to dip or sink, so the core picture is something rising out of the water into view.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词由 e-（向外）与 mergere（浸入、下沉）组合，核心画面就是某物从水里升起、露出水面。

senses.title: To become known
senses.definition: to become known or apparent after being hidden or unclear
senses.definitionCN: 原本隐藏或不清晰的事情变得为人所知
senses.example: New facts emerged during the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 审判过程中有新的情况显露出来。
senses.why: Facts can rise out of obscurity just as an object rises out of water, so the physical surfacing becomes a metaphor for disclosure.
senses.whyCN: 事实能像物体升出水面一样从模糊中浮现，于是这个物理动作变成了「真相显露」的比喻。

senses.title: To come into existence
senses.definition: to begin to exist or become established
senses.definitionCN: 开始存在或逐渐确立
senses.example: A new industry emerged in the coastal city.
senses.exampleCN: 一座新兴产业在这座沿海城市兴起。
senses.why: What rises into view did not exist for the observer before, so emergence also names the birth of a thing or trend.
senses.whyCN: 对观察者来说，升起并进入视野的东西此前并不存在，所以 emergence 也用来命名事物或趋势的诞生。

senses.title: To survive a difficult period
senses.definition: to come out of a difficult experience in a new or stronger position
senses.definitionCN: 从艰难经历中走出来，处于新的或更强的位置
senses.example: The small firm emerged stronger after the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 危机之后这家小公司变得更强。
senses.why: Coming out of water is also coming out of danger, so the verb describes a person or group that survives a trial and steps into the open.
senses.whyCN: 从水里出来也意味着从危险中出来，所以这个动词形容人或群体熬过考验、走到开阔处。

intro.en: Emerge comes straight from Latin emergere, to rise out of a liquid.
intro.cn: emerge 直接来自拉丁语 emergere，意为从液体中升起。

items.en: Mergere meant to dip, plunge or sink.
items.cn: mergere 意为浸入、扎入或下沉。

items.en: With e-, out, the verb meant to rise out of water.
items.cn: 加上 e-（向外）后，动词意为从水中升起。

items.en: The participle described something coming up into view.
items.cn: 其分词形容某物升上来、进入视野。

items.en: English borrowed the verb for physical surfacing.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入该动词，表示物理上的浮出。

items.en: The sense widened to facts becoming known and new things coming into being.
items.cn: 词义扩大到事实显露与新事物产生。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the merge root and its derived nouns; the near-meaning group separates appearing, surfacing and arising.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 merge 词根及其派生名词展开；近义组区分出现、浮出水面与产生。

entries.definition: The process of coming out or into existence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「出现、兴起」的过程。

entries.definition: Newly appearing or developing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「新兴的、刚出现的」。

entries.definition: To sink into or combine, from the same Latin verb without e-.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「合并、融入」，同一个拉丁动词去掉 e- 前缀。

entries.definition: To become visible, often without effort.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「出现」，常不带努力感。

entries.definition: To come up to the top, literally or figuratively.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「浮出水面」，可实指也可比喻。

entries.definition: To begin to exist, especially of problems or situations.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「产生」，多用于问题或局面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks read emerge as e- plus merge, out of the dip, then let the same rise become truth and new life.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 emerge 读成 e- 加 merge，即「从浸没中出来」，再让这次上升变成真相与新事物。

normal.en: E- means out and merge means sink, so emerge means rise out.
normal.cn: e- 表示向外，merge 表示下沉，所以 emerge 就是升出来。

normal.en: The sun emerges from the clouds.
normal.cn: 太阳从云层里露出来。

normal.en: Facts emerge when the water of secrecy drops.
normal.cn: 保密的水位一降，事实就露出来。

normal.en: A new market can emerge overnight.
normal.cn: 新市场可以在一夜之间兴起。

normal.en: A team can emerge stronger from a crisis.
normal.cn: 一个团队能从危机中变得更强。

abstract.en: Picture a dark shape rising slowly through water.
abstract.cn: 想象一团黑影从水下慢慢升起。

abstract.en: What was hidden becomes visible, and what did not exist begins to be.
abstract.cn: 藏着的东西变得可见，不存在的东西开始存在。

abstract.en: Emerge is a birth told as a surfacing.
abstract.cn: emerge 就是把诞生讲成一次浮出水面。

examples.en: The sun emerged from behind the clouds.
examples.cn: 太阳从云层后露出。

examples.en: New facts emerged during the trial.
examples.cn: 审判过程中有新的情况显露出来。

examples.en: The small firm emerged stronger after the crisis.
examples.cn: 危机之后这家小公司变得更强。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一默己」——水下一声不响，忽然露头

root: 拉丁语 emergere，由 e-（向外）加 mergere（浸入、下沉）构成，字面为「从水中升起」。

sensesIntro.en: Emerge rises from water into sight, then into knowledge, then into existence, and finally out of danger.
sensesIntro.cn: emerge 先从水里升到视野中，再升到知识里，再升成新事物，最后升出危险。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shape rising through dark water until it breaks the surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团影子从暗水中升起，直到破开水面。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: the sun or a swimmer comes up.
branches.cn: 水面线：太阳或游泳者升出水面。

branches.en: THE TRUTH: hidden facts rise into view.
branches.cn: 真相线：隐藏的事实升入视野。

branches.en: THE NEW THING: an industry or trend begins.
branches.cn: 新事物线：产业或趋势开始出现。

branches.en: THE SURVIVOR: a person or firm comes out stronger.
branches.cn: 幸存线：人或公司更强地走出来。

branches.en: ONE RISE: water, truth and history share the same motion.
branches.cn: 同一次上升：水面、真相与历史共享同一个动作。

intro.en: Emerge is e-, out, plus the Latin root merg, sink, with the English verb ending -e.
intro.cn: emerge 是 e-（向外）加拉丁词根 merg（下沉），再接英语动词词尾 -e。

latinIntro.en: Mergere and emergere are both recorded Latin verbs of dipping and rising.
latinIntro.cn: mergere 与 emergere 都是有记录的拉丁语动词，分别表示浸入与升起。

definition_zh: 巨大的；广阔的；浩瀚的；大量的、极多的
definition_en: extremely large in area, amount or degree
core_image: 站在沙丘顶端望出去，地平线一直退到眼睛看不见的地方
scene: 夜里没有一盏灯，抬头只看见铺满星星的天。 A vast plain stretched away in every direction.
sceneCN: 这里 vast 是「广阔的、浩瀚的」（第 1 个义项：面积极大）；句意为一片广阔的平原向四面八方伸展开去。地平线退到看不见的地方，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：巨大的、广阔的、浩瀚的；大量的

derivatives.zh: 副词，义为「极大地、远远地」，如 vastly improved
名词，书面说法，义为「广袤」，较少使用

senses.title: Enormous in area
senses.titleCN: 面积巨大：眼睛望不到边
senses.definition: extremely large in area or extent
senses.definitionCN: 面积或范围极大
senses.example: A vast plain stretched away in every direction.
senses.exampleCN: 一片广阔的平原向四面八方伸展开去。
senses.why: Latin vastus meant empty and desolate; the emptiness itself is what takes the breath away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vastus 意为空旷荒芜；正是这种空旷让人屏息。

senses.title: Enormous in amount
senses.titleCN: 数量巨大：多到难以清点
senses.definition: extremely large in number or quantity
senses.definitionCN: 数量或数目极大
senses.example: A vast amount of data was collected over ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 十年间收集了海量的数据。
senses.why: The word moves from space to quantity: numbers can also open out like a plain.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从空间移到数量：数字也能像平原一样铺开。

senses.title: Great in degree
senses.titleCN: 程度巨大：差别或优势悬殊
senses.definition: very great in degree, used of differences and advantages
senses.definitionCN: 在程度上非常大，用于差别与优势
senses.example: There is a vast difference between the two plans.
senses.exampleCN: 两个方案之间差别巨大。
senses.why: Here the size is abstract: not metres but distance in quality or outcome.
senses.whyCN: 这里的大小是抽象的：量的是质量或结果上的距离，而非米数。

senses.title: The great majority
senses.titleCN: 绝大多数：人群中的绝大部分
senses.definition: used with majority to mean almost all
senses.definitionCN: 与 majority 连用，表示几乎全部
senses.example: The vast majority of students passed the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 绝大多数学生通过了考试。
senses.why: A crowd can be vast too; the same word measures people.
senses.whyCN: 人群也可以是 vast；同一个词也能量人。

intro.en: Vast comes from Latin vastus, empty and desolate, which already described land that stretched out bare.
intro.cn: vast 来自拉丁语 vastus「空旷荒芜的」，本已形容光秃秃铺展开的土地。

items.en: The adjective vastus meant empty, waste or desolate, applied to ruined land.
items.cn: 形容词 vastus 意为空旷的、荒废的、荒凉的，用于被毁坏的土地。

items.en: Its verb vastare meant to lay waste, and lies behind English waste and devastate.
items.cn: 其动词 vastare 意为摧残荒废，是英语 waste 与 devastate 的来源。

items.en: Old French vaste kept the sense of wide and unoccupied space.
items.cn: 古法语 vaste 保留了辽阔空旷的意思。

items.en: English borrowed vast in the fifteenth century for enormous extent.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 vast，表示范围极大。

items.en: Modern usage extends it from land to amounts and differences, while the sense of emptiness fades.
items.cn: 现代用法把它从土地扩展到数量与差别，同时「空旷」的感觉渐渐淡去。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem of waste and emptiness; the near-meaning group holds words for great size.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示「荒废、空」的拉丁词干；近义组收表示巨大的词。

entries.definition: By a very large amount; the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「极大地」，是本词的副词形式。

entries.definition: The quality of being vast; the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广阔」，是本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: To lay waste or ruin; uses the Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「毁坏」，出自同一拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Empty or unused land; a distant English cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「荒地、浪费」，英语里的远亲。

entries.definition: Very large in size, plainer and more everyday.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「巨大的」，更日常。

entries.definition: So large it cannot be measured; close in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无边的」，语气接近。

entries.definition: Larger than normal, with a hint of shock.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「庞大的」，带惊奇感。

entries.definition: Having no limits, stressing no edge rather than size.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无边无际的」，强调没有边界。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the empty-plain core and real collocations like vast majority.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「空旷平原」意象与 vast majority 这类真实搭配。

normal.en: Vast majority means almost all, not merely most.
normal.cn: vast majority 指几乎全部，不只是大多数。

normal.en: Vast came from a Latin word for empty land.
normal.cn: vast 来自拉丁语中表示空地的词。

normal.en: Vast difference is a huge gap, not a big object.
normal.cn: vast difference 指巨大差距，不是巨大物件。

normal.en: Vaster and vastest exist, though writers often use more vast.
normal.cn: vaster 与 vastest 存在，但作家常用 more vast。

normal.en: Vastly improved means improved by a very large amount.
normal.cn: vastly improved 指改善幅度极大。

abstract.en: Vast began as emptiness and became size: the feeling of distance is older than the measure of it.
abstract.cn: vast 从「空」长成「大」：对距离的感受比测量更古老。

abstract.en: Something vast makes the viewer small, which is why the word always carries a trace of awe.
abstract.cn: 巨大之物让人显小，所以这个词总带一丝敬畏。

abstract.en: The same word measures land, data and differences, because largeness is a comparison, not a substance.
abstract.cn: 同一个词量土地、数据与差别，因为「大」是比较，不是实体。

examples.en: Vast areas of the country remain uninhabited.
examples.cn: 这个国家的大片地区仍无人居住。

examples.en: She spent a vast amount of time on the research.
examples.cn: 她在这项研究上花了大量时间。

examples.en: The vast majority of customers were satisfied.
examples.cn: 绝大多数顾客表示满意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哇死他」——哇，他一个人管那么大一片地：广阔的

root: 源自拉丁语形容词 vastus「空旷荒芜的」及其动词 vastare「荒废」，经古法语 vaste 于十五世纪进入英语；同族词有 devastate、waste。

sensesIntro.en: Vast starts with land that has no edge, then measures quantities, differences and the bulk of a crowd.
sensesIntro.cn: vast 从望不到边的土地开始，然后用来量数量、差别与人群的绝大部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a horizon that keeps moving back as you look at it.
core.cn: 核心意象：你越看，那条地平线退得越远。

branches.en: SPACE LINE: land and water without visible edge.
branches.cn: 空间线：看不见边际的陆地与水面。

branches.en: QUANTITY LINE: numbers or data in huge bulk.
branches.cn: 数量线：成堆的数字与数据。

branches.en: DEGREE LINE: a gap that feels like distance.
branches.cn: 程度线：像距离一样的悬殊。

branches.en: CROWD LINE: nearly all the people counted.
branches.cn: 人群线：被计数的人几乎全部。

branches.en: CONTRAST: huge is a size, vast is a stretch.
branches.cn: 对照线：huge 指尺寸，vast 指铺展。

intro.en: Vast is a whole Latin stem; its English relatives take -ly and -ness, while devastate keeps the Latin verb.
intro.cn: vast 是完整的拉丁词干，英语亲属词接 -ly 与 -ness，而 devastate 保留拉丁动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pair is the adjective vastus and the verb vastare, both about emptiness and ruin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的一对是形容词 vastus 与动词 vastare，都与空旷和毁坏有关。

items.example: It shows the old root in English.
items.exampleCN: 它在英语里展示这个老词根。

definition_zh: 有意识的；清醒的；察觉到的；刻意的
definition_en: awake and able to think, aware of something, or done on purpose
core_image: 病房里，病人睁开眼，第一次看清天花板
scene: 病人睁眼后先看清天花板，再认出床边的人。 She was conscious of every sound in the room.
sceneCN: 这里 conscious 指「察觉到的」（第 2 个义项：意识到某事存在）；句意是她察觉到房间里的每一种声音。

pos.zh: 有意识的；清醒的；察觉的；刻意的

senses.title: Awake and aware
senses.definition: awake and able to think and feel
senses.definitionCN: 醒着，能够思考与感受
senses.example: The patient was conscious after the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术之后病人是清醒的。
senses.why: The light is on behind the eyes again.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛后面的灯，又亮起来了。

senses.title: Noticing something
senses.definition: noticing that something exists or is happening
senses.definitionCN: 注意到某事物的存在或正在发生
senses.example: She was conscious of every sound in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她察觉到房间里的每一种声音。
senses.why: Attention turns a background noise into a fact you must answer.
senses.whyCN: 注意力把背景里的声音，变成你必须回应的事实。

senses.title: Done on purpose
senses.definition: deliberate and intended rather than accidental
senses.definitionCN: 有意为之，而非偶然发生
senses.example: He made a conscious effort to slow down.
senses.exampleCN: 他刻意放慢了速度。
senses.why: A choice you can see yourself making is a choice you own.
senses.whyCN: 你能看见自己做出的选择，才是你真正拥有的选择。

intro.en: Conscious comes from Latin conscius, knowing with others or within oneself, from com-, with, and scire, to know.
intro.cn: conscious 来自拉丁语 conscius，意为与他人或与自己共知，由 com-（与）与 scire（知道）构成。

items.en: Scire meant to know, and conscius meant sharing that knowledge.
items.cn: scire 意为知道，conscius 意为共享这份知识。

items.en: A conscious person was one who knew a thing with another.
items.cn: conscius 的人，是与另一个人共同知道某事的人。

items.en: Later the knowing turned inward, meaning aware of oneself.
items.cn: 后来这种知道转向内部，表示对自身的察觉。

items.en: English conscious first meant sharing knowledge of something.
items.cn: 英语 conscious 最初指对某事知情。

items.en: It settled into the modern sense of awake and aware.
items.cn: 它逐渐固定为清醒而有察觉的现代含义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the conscience family, and the meaning group names other words for being aware or deliberate.
note.cn: 形近组是 conscience 家族，近义组列出其他表示察觉或刻意的词。

entries.definition: the inner sense of right and wrong
the state of being awake and aware
careful to do things properly
knowing that something exists
not asleep
done on purpose

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from eyes opening in a hospital bed, then move to a sound you cannot ignore and to a step you choose to take.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从病床上睁开的眼睛开始，再到无法忽略的声音，最后到你选择迈出的一步。

normal.en: Con- is with and sci- is know, so conscious is knowing with your own mind.
normal.cn: con- 是与，sci- 是知道，conscious 就是用自己的心智去知道。

normal.en: Waking up is the first conscious moment of the day.
normal.cn: 醒来，是一天中第一个有意识的时刻。

normal.en: To be conscious of a sound is to let it into your mind.
normal.cn: 察觉到一种声音，就是让它进入你的头脑。

normal.en: A conscious choice leaves a footprint you can point to.
normal.cn: 有意的选择，会留下一个你能指出的脚印。

normal.en: Half awake is not conscious enough to drive.
normal.cn: 半睡半醒，还没清醒到可以开车。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp switching on above a bed.
abstract.cn: 想象床头上方一盏灯被打开。

abstract.en: Picture a finger lifted to say wait a moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指举起来，示意稍等。

abstract.en: Picture a foot placed slowly and on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚缓慢而刻意地落下。

examples.en: He was conscious during the whole flight.
examples.cn: 整个飞行途中他都是清醒的。

examples.en: I am conscious of my own limits.
examples.cn: 我清楚自己的限度。

examples.en: She made a conscious choice to stay.
examples.cn: 她是有意选择留下来的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conscious 记成 con（与自己一起）加 sci（知道）加 ous（形容词）：心里明白自己与周围在发生什么，就是有意识。

root: 源自拉丁语 conscius（com 与 + scire 知道），本义是共知，后转为对自身与周围有察觉，并引申出刻意的含义。

sensesIntro.en: From eyes opening, to a sound entering the mind, and finally to a step taken on purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: 从眼睛睁开，到声音进入头脑，最后到刻意迈出的一步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp switched on behind the eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：眼睛后面有一盏灯被点亮。

branches.en: The first sense is simply being awake and able to think.
branches.cn: 第一个义项只是醒着并能思考。

branches.en: The second sense points outward at something noticed.
branches.cn: 第二个义项目光向外，指向被注意到的事物。

branches.en: The third sense turns awareness into a chosen act.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把觉察变成有意的行动。

branches.en: You must be awake before anything can be noticed.
branches.cn: 必须先醒着，才可能注意到什么。

branches.en: Noticing a habit is the first step to changing it on purpose.
branches.cn: 察觉一个习惯，是刻意改变它的第一步。

intro.en: Conscious is built on Latin com-, with, plus scire, to know, and the adjective ending -ous.
intro.cn: conscious 由拉丁语 com-（与）与 scire（知道）加上形容词词尾 -ous 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin know base sci- also appears in science, conscience and omniscient.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的知道词基 sci- 也出现在 science、conscience 与 omniscient 中。

items.exampleCN: 药物让他的意识变得迟钝。

items.example: He was unconscious on the floor.
items.exampleCN: 他倒在地板上失去了知觉。

items.example: A subconscious habit shaped her choice.
items.exampleCN: 一个潜意识习惯塑造了她的选择。

items.meaning: the inner sense of right and wrong

items.exampleCN: 没有哪位老师无所不知。

definition_zh: 在…之内；在…以内；（时间上）不超过；在内部
definition_en: inside a place, a group or a limit, or before a period of time has come to an end
core_image: 院子四周围着矮墙，墙里的地方全都算在内，墙外一步就出了界限
scene: 医生交代，这片药必须在一周之内吃完，超过了就得重来。 Please reply within three days of receiving this letter.
sceneCN: 这里 within 是「在…之内、不超过」（第 1 个义项：在某范围或期限之内）；句意为请在收到此信后三天内回复。矮墙围出的那块地方，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Inside a space or a group
senses.definition: inside the limits of a place, a group or an area
senses.definitionCN: 在某地、某群体或某区域的范围之内
senses.example: There are three small rooms within the tower.
senses.exampleCN: 塔里有三个小房间。
senses.why: The word began as with plus in, so the picture is a space with everything kept inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是 with 加 in，画面是一个把一切都围在里面的空间。

senses.title: Before a period ends
senses.definition: before the end of a stated period of time, so the limit is never exceeded
senses.definitionCN: 在说明的这段时间结束之前，绝不超出这个限度
senses.example: Please reply within three days of receiving this letter.
senses.exampleCN: 请在收到此信后三天内回复。
senses.why: Time was treated as a space with a boundary, and staying inside it means finishing before the end.
senses.whyCN: 时间被当成一个有边界的空间，待在里面就是按时完成。

senses.title: Inside a set of rules or limits
senses.definition: inside the limits allowed by a rule, a law or an ability
senses.definitionCN: 在规则、法律或能力允许的限度之内
senses.example: The price is within the range we agreed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个价格在我们商定的范围内。
senses.why: A rule is a wall you may move inside but not cross, so the same word serves for law and ability.
senses.whyCN: 规则是一道可以活动却不能越过的墙，所以这个词也用于法律与能力。

senses.title: From inside a place
senses.definition: used after from to show a movement that starts inside something
senses.definitionCN: 用在 from 之后，表示动作从某物内部开始
senses.example: The decision was made from within the village itself.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定是从村子内部做出的。
senses.why: When the boundary is the point, the adverb can stand alone to say inside or from inside.
senses.whyCN: 当边界本身成为重点，这个副词可以单独使用，表示在里面或从里面。

intro.en: Within started as with plus in, two prepositions stacked, and became a single word meaning inside a boundary.
intro.cn: within 起初是 with 加 in，两个介词叠用，后来合为一个词，意为在边界之内。

items.en: The two words wið and inn were written together when they marked a place kept inside.
items.cn: wið 与 inn 两词在标记「围在里面」时开始连写。

items.en: The compound meant literally inside, with the inside itself as the focus.
items.cn: 这个复合词字面意为在里面，重点落在内部本身。

items.en: withinne became within, and time limits joined place limits.
items.cn: withinne 变作 within，时间界限与空间界限并列。

items.en: The word became the standard form for a limit that must not be crossed.
items.cn: 这个词成了「不得越过的界限」的标准形式。

items.en: From within and within reach fixed the word in daily phrases.
items.cn: from within 与 within reach 让这个词固定在日常短语里。

note.en: The first group holds close matches in form and meaning, the second words for limits and space.
note.cn: 第一组收形义都相近的词，第二组收表示限度与空间的词。

Together with.

normalIntro.en: Within is with plus in, a pair of words folded into one, and the picture is a boundary you stay inside.
normalIntro.cn: within 是 with 加 in 两个词折成一个，画面是你待在里面的那道边界。

normal.en: It looks like with plus an n: the n of in was kept.
normal.cn: 它看起来像 with 加一个 n：in 的 n 被保留了下来。

normal.en: Without is its mirror image: both start with with.
normal.cn: without 是它的镜像：两个都以 with 开头。

normal.en: Within a week means last day included, not the day after.
normal.cn: within a week 意为最晚到那天，不含之后。

normal.en: Within reach is the arm's length as a boundary.
normal.cn: within reach 就是一条手臂长的那道边界。

normal.en: Write from within when the starting point is inside.
normal.cn: 当起点在内部，就用 from within。

abstract.en: A low wall and everything the wall keeps together.
abstract.cn: 一道矮墙，以及墙里聚在一起的一切。

abstract.en: A circle drawn in sand, with both feet inside it.
abstract.cn: 沙地上画的一个圈，两只脚都在圈内。

abstract.en: A clock whose hands have not reached the mark.
abstract.cn: 一只时针还没到刻度的钟。

examples.en: The package will arrive within four working days.
examples.cn: 包裹将在四个工作日内送达。

examples.en: The village lies within sight of the sea.
examples.cn: 村子就在能看见海的范围之内。

examples.en: We must keep our spending within the budget.
examples.cn: 我们必须把开支控制在预算之内。

dict_mnemonic.text: with + in —— 两词合起来：在这个范围「里面」。

root: 古英语 wið + inn（with + in）→ withinne → within；反义相关形式有 without。

sensesIntro.en: A space with a kept-inside boundary becomes a deadline, then a rule, and finally can stand alone as the inside itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个围出内部的边界变成期限，再变成规则，最后可以单独指内部本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a low wall with everything on the inner side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道矮墙，墙内的一切。

branches.en: The place branch: three rooms inside the tower.
branches.cn: 空间分支：塔里的三个房间。

branches.en: The time branch: a reply due in three days.
branches.cn: 时间分支：三天内回复。

branches.en: The limit branch: a price inside the agreed range.
branches.cn: 限度分支：落在商定区间内的价格。

branches.en: The adverb branch: a choice made from inside.
branches.cn: 副词分支：从内部做出的决定。

branches.en: The keep-inside branch: do not cross, do not overrun.
branches.cn: 守界分支：别越过，别超支。

intro.en: Within is a fused compound of two native prepositions, with and in, and its mirror word is without.
intro.cn: within 是 with 与 in 两个本土介词熔成的复合词，它的镜像词是 without。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; the Latin entries are borrowed prepositions for inside and within.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语；拉丁条目是表示内部的借入介词。

The second half, with its n kept.
items.exampleCN: 后半，保留了自己的 n。

items.example: The same two pieces turned outward.
A formal cousin of the same idea.

A body measure used as a limit.
The boundary seen as a starting point.

definition_zh: 路线；路径；途径；按路线发送
definition_en: the way from one place to another, a way to achieve something, or to send along a chosen way
core_image: 地图上被红线标出的道路
scene: 司机选了一条避开拥堵的路线。 The driver chose a route that avoided the traffic.
sceneCN: 这里 route 是「路线」（第 1 个义项）；句意：司机选了一条避开拥堵的路线。

senses.title: Way to a place
senses.definition: the way that you take to get from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一个地方到另一个地方所走的路径
senses.example: The mountain route is shorter but steeper.
senses.exampleCN: 山路更短，但更陡。
senses.why: A line on the map joins two places.
senses.whyCN: 地图上的线把两个地方连起来。

senses.title: Way to a goal
senses.definition: a way of achieving something
senses.definitionCN: 达成某事的办法或渠道
senses.example: Hard work is the surest route to success.
senses.exampleCN: 努力是通往成功最可靠的途径。
senses.why: The path image moves from land to life.
senses.whyCN: 道路的意象从地理移到人生。

senses.title: Send along
senses.definition: to send something by a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 按特定路径发送某物
senses.example: The goods were routed through the north port.
senses.exampleCN: 货物经北方港口转运。
senses.why: The noun becomes the act of choosing the path.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成选择路径的动作。

intro.en: Route comes from Latin rupta via, a broken or cleared way.
intro.cn: route 源自拉丁语 rupta via，意为开辟出来的道路。

items.en: Rupta means broken or cleared.
items.cn: rupta 意为破开的、开辟的。

items.en: Rupta via names a cleared road.
items.cn: rupta via 指开辟出来的路。

items.en: Old French rute keeps the road sense.
items.cn: 古法语 rute 保留道路含义。

items.en: English route names a chosen way.
items.cn: 英语 route 指选定的路径。

items.en: Route also means a way to a goal.
items.cn: route 又指达到目标的途径。

note.en: A route is a way; a root is the base of a plant.
note.cn: route 是路线，root 则是植物的根。

entries.definition: the underground part of a plant
a complete defeat
a device that directs network traffic
a way laid out for walking
a method or road
the direction something follows

normalIntro.en: A route is the line you follow to arrive.
normalIntro.cn: route 是你一路跟随、最终抵达的那条线。

normal.en: This bus route passes the station.
normal.cn: 这条公交线路经过车站。

normal.en: We took the coastal route to save time.
normal.cn: 我们走海边路线以节省时间。

normal.en: The map shows a route to the peak.
normal.cn: 地图标出了通往山顶的路线。

normal.en: They found an escape route through the woods.
normal.cn: 他们找到一条穿过树林的逃生路线。

normal.en: The plane stopped en route to Paris.
normal.cn: 飞机在飞往巴黎途中停留。

abstract.en: Picture a red line drawn across a map.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上画出的一条红线。

abstract.en: Imagine footprints leading from one town to another.
abstract.cn: 想象脚印从一个城镇通向另一个。

abstract.en: Think of a signpost pointing down a clear road.
abstract.cn: 想象路标指向一条清晰的道路。

examples.en: The driver took the shortest route home.
examples.cn: 司机走了回家最短的路线。

examples.en: Education is a route out of poverty.
examples.cn: 教育是摆脱贫困的一条途径。

examples.en: All calls are routed through one office.
examples.cn: 所有电话都经一个办公室转接。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「route」和「root」同音——树有根，路也有根：那条从起点长到终点的线，就是路线。

root: 拉丁语 rupta via（开辟出的道路）→ 古法语 rute → route，核心义「打通出来、可以通行的线」。

sensesIntro.en: Route means a way between places, a way to a goal, or to send by a chosen way.
sensesIntro.cn: route 意为两地之间的路线、达成目标的途径，或按路线发送。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red line across a map.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上的一条红线。

branches.en: The physical way is the first sense.
branches.cn: 实际道路是第一个义项。

branches.en: The path becomes a method in life.
branches.cn: 道路变成人生中的方法。

branches.en: The verb sends things along a path.
branches.cn: 动词让货物沿路径发送。

branches.en: Both lead from a start to a goal.
branches.cn: 两者都从起点通向目标。

branches.en: The path can be walked or assigned.
branches.cn: 路径既可以走，也可以被安排。

intro.en: Route goes back to Latin rupta via, a cleared road.
intro.cn: route 追溯到拉丁语 rupta via，意为开辟出来的道路。

latinIntro.en: Rupta via gives French rute and English route.
latinIntro.cn: rupta via 给出法语 rute 与英语 route。

items.example: Route keeps the open road image.

items.exampleCN: reroute 意为重新选择路线。

latinEntries.example: Rupta is part of the source phrase.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rupta 是来源短语的一部分。

definition_zh: 目标；靶子；把……作为目标
definition_en: an object aimed at, a goal, or to make something the aim of an action
core_image: 箭簇正插在靶心的红圈里
scene: 第一支箭就射中了靶子的中心。 The first arrow hit the centre of the target.
sceneCN: 这里 target 是「靶子」（第 1 个义项）；句意：第一支箭就射中了靶子的中心。

senses.title: A mark to shoot at
senses.definition: a board or object marked with rings for shooting at
senses.definitionCN: 画有圆环、供射击的板或物
senses.example: The first arrow hit the centre of the target.
senses.exampleCN: 第一支箭就射中了靶子的中心。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the small round shield used for practice.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项是练习用的小圆盾，靶子由此而来。

senses.title: A goal to reach
senses.definition: a result that a person or group aims to achieve
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体想要达到的结果
senses.example: The team met its sales target this year.
senses.exampleCN: 团队今年完成了销售目标。
senses.why: A goal is a target you shoot at with effort rather than an arrow.
senses.whyCN: 目标就是你用努力而非箭去射的那个靶。

senses.title: To aim at something
senses.definition: to direct an action or effort toward a particular group or thing
senses.definitionCN: 把行动或精力对准某个群体或事物
senses.example: The campaign targets young voters.
senses.exampleCN: 这场活动针对年轻选民。
senses.why: The noun turned into the act of aiming.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成了「瞄准」这个动作。

intro.en: Target came from a small shield carried in practice.
intro.cn: target 源自练习时用的那种小圆盾。

items.en: Targette was a small shield.
items.cn: targette 意为小盾。

items.en: Target named a light round shield.
items.cn: target 指轻便的圆盾。

items.en: Target became the mark for shooting.
items.cn: target 变成射击的靶子。

items.en: It extended to goals in business and study.
items.cn: 它扩展到商业与学业中的目标。

items.en: The verb means aiming effort at something.
items.cn: 动词义为把精力对准某物。

note.en: Target is compared with look-alike forms and with words for goals.
note.cn: 把 target 与形近形式以及表示目标的词作对比。

abstract.cn: 练习场上的盾，成了人生里的目标。

abstract.en: Aim turns an object into a purpose.
abstract.cn: 瞄准把一个物件变成一种目的。

abstract.en: Every target is a promise of direction.
abstract.cn: 每个目标都是一份方向的承诺。

examples.en: The first arrow hit the centre of the target.
examples.cn: 第一支箭就射中了靶子的中心。

examples.en: The team met its sales target this year.
examples.cn: 团队今年完成了销售目标。

examples.en: The campaign targets young voters.
examples.cn: 这场活动针对年轻选民。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「他个头」——瞄准「他个头」那么高的小圆牌，就是靶子。

root: 古法语 targette（小盾），进入英语后由「练习用盾」转为「靶子」，再引申为「目标」。

sensesIntro.en: Target moves from a practice shield to a shooting mark to any goal and the act of aiming.
sensesIntro.cn: target 从练习用盾，到射击靶，再到任何目标与瞄准的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow standing in a red centre.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支箭钉在红色靶心上。

branches.en: The shooting mark is the base sense.
branches.cn: 射击靶是基础义项。

branches.en: A goal is a target for effort.
branches.cn: 目标是努力的靶。

branches.en: The verb is the act of aiming.
branches.cn: 动词是瞄准的动作。

branches.en: Both are things aimed at.
branches.cn: 两者都是被瞄准之物。

branches.en: Planning and aiming belong together.
branches.cn: 规划与瞄准本是一体。

intro.en: Target forms a modern family of aiming words.
intro.cn: target 形成一组关于瞄准的现代词族。

latinIntro.en: Target comes from Old French, ultimately from a shield word.
latinIntro.cn: target 来自古法语，根源是表示盾的词。

definition_zh: 出现；发生；（问题）产生；起因于；起身；起立
definition_en: to come into being, especially as a problem or situation; to result from something; or to stand up
core_image: 地面裂开一道缝，一个问题从里面冒出来
scene: 清晨工地，工程师蹲下查看地面的一道裂缝。 New problems arise whenever the rain stops the work.
sceneCN: 这里 arise 是「出现；发生」（第 1 个义项：某事开始存在、冒出来）；句意为「每逢下雨停工，新问题就会出现」。画面里有清晨工地、地面裂缝与蹲下查看的工程师。

pos.zh: 动词：出现；发生；产生；起因于；起身

derivatives.zh: 与本词同源的动词，义为「升起；上升」
由 sun 与 rise 复合，义为「日出」
由 up 与 rise 复合，义为「起义；升起」

senses.title: To come into being
senses.definition: to come into being, especially as a problem, question, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 开始存在，尤指问题、疑问或状况冒出来
senses.example: New problems arise whenever the rain stops the work.
senses.exampleCN: 每逢下雨停工，新问题就会出现。
senses.why: Old English arisan meant to rise up; what arises rises into view from where it was hidden.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 arisan 意为升起；出现的东西，是从原本藏身之处升到视野里的。

senses.title: To result from a cause
senses.definition: to result or proceed from a particular cause or source
senses.definitionCN: 由某个特定的原因或源头产生
senses.example: Most of the delays arise from poor planning.
senses.exampleCN: 多数延误都源于规划不周。
senses.why: If a thing rises out of a source, the source is what it grows from.
senses.whyCN: 若一物从某个源头升起，那个源头就是它长出来的地方。

senses.title: To stand up
senses.definition: to stand up, especially in a formal or old-fashioned context
senses.definitionCN: 站起身来，尤用于正式或较古的语境
senses.example: The assembly arose as one when the judge entered.
senses.exampleCN: 法官进来时，全场一致起立。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense: the body itself rises.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的身体义：身体本身升起来。

senses.title: To come up as a need
senses.definition: in the phrase when the need arises, to come up as a need at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 when the need arises，指需要在其时刻出现
senses.example: We will call you when the need arises.
senses.exampleCN: 有需要时我们会打电话给你。
senses.why: A need is another thing that rises into view when its moment comes.
senses.whyCN: 需求也是在其时刻到来时升入视野的东西。

intro.en: Arise is a native Germanic verb of rising, and its abstract senses grow out of that upward motion.
intro.cn: arise 是本土的日耳曼语动词，本义为升起，抽象义都从这股向上的动作长出来。

items.en: 「*rīsan」 'to rise' is reconstructed; the a- prefix adds the idea of up and out.
items.cn: 「*rīsan」意为「升起」，是重构形式；a- 前缀带来向上、向外的意思。

items.en: Arisan means 'to rise up, get up', used of people and of events alike.
items.cn: arisan 意为「升起、起身」，人和事件都可以用它。

items.en: The verb keeps both the bodily sense and the sense of something coming up.
items.cn: 这个动词同时保留身体义与某事冒出来的意思。

items.en: The sense of resulting from a cause becomes common in careful prose.
items.cn: 「由某个原因引起」的义项在讲究的文字里变得常见。

items.en: Arise is now mostly formal and mostly about problems, questions and needs.
items.cn: 现代 arise 多用于正式语体，也多与问题、疑问和需求连用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same irregular verb; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of appearing and resulting.
note.cn: 形近组收同一不规则动词的各形态；近义组收表示出现与由来的动词。

entries.definition: The past tense of arise.
entries.definitionCN: arise 的过去式，义为「出现了；起身了」。

entries.definition: The past participle of arise.
entries.definitionCN: arise 的过去分词，搭配 have 或 be 使用。

entries.definition: The present participle of arise.
entries.definitionCN: arise 的现在分词，义为「正在出现的」。

entries.definition: To move upward or increase.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「升起、上升」，与 arise 同源。

entries.definition: To come out and become visible.
entries.definitionCN: 出现并变得可见，比 arise 更强调从隐藏处出来。

entries.definition: To happen or take place.
entries.definitionCN: 发生，对应 arise 的事件义。

entries.definition: To come into sight.
entries.definitionCN: 进入视野，与 arise 的「冒出」义接近。

entries.definition: To come about as a consequence.
entries.definitionCN: 作为结果产生，对应 arise from 的起因义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the upward motion of rising, then let it produce problems and needs.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子保留「升起」这个向上动作，再让它生出问题与需求。

normal.en: Arise is a kind of rising: something comes up into view.
normal.cn: arise 是一种升起：某物升入视野。

normal.en: A problem rises out of the ground.
normal.cn: 问题从地面升起来。

normal.en: A delay rises out of its cause.
normal.cn: 延误从它的原因里升起来。

normal.en: A person rises to the feet: the oldest sense.
normal.cn: 人升到双脚站立：最古老的义项。

normal.en: A need rises when its moment comes.
normal.cn: 需求在它的时刻到来时升起。

abstract.en: Everything that begins is pictured as rising.
abstract.cn: 一切开始存在的东西，都被想象成升起。

abstract.en: The word makes causes look like ground.
abstract.cn: 这个词把原因看成土地。

abstract.en: Its formality suits troubles more than joys.
abstract.cn: 它的正式语体更适合麻烦，而不是喜悦。

examples.en: New problems arise whenever the rain stops the work.
examples.cn: 每逢下雨停工，新问题就会出现。

examples.en: Most of the delays arise from poor planning.
examples.cn: 多数延误都源于规划不周。

examples.en: The assembly arose as one when the judge entered.
examples.cn: 法官进来时，全场一致起立。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿莱兹」——地面裂开，问题从缝里升起来：出现；发生

root: arise 是本土的日耳曼语动词，来自古英语 arisan「升起、起身」，源头可追到原始日耳曼语的重构形式。它的核心动作是向上：人从坐姿升到站立，就是起身；一件事从原本藏身的地方升到视野里，就是出现与发生；一件事从某个源头升出来，就是由那个原因引起。现代英语里，这个词多用于正式语体，最常与问题、疑问和需求搭配。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses all involve something rising: a problem appearing, a result coming from a cause, a body standing up, and a need coming at its time.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法都涉及某物升起：问题出现、结果从原因而来、身体站起，以及需求在特定时刻到来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crack opening in the ground, and something rising out of it.
core.cn: 核心意象：地面裂开一道缝，有东西从缝里升上来。

branches.en: THE APPEARANCE LINE: a problem rises into view.
branches.cn: 出现线：问题升入视野。

branches.en: THE SOURCE LINE: a result rises out of its cause.
branches.cn: 来源线：结果从原因里升出来。

branches.en: THE BODY LINE: the oldest sense is standing up.
branches.cn: 身体线：最古老的义项是站起。

branches.en: THE NEED LINE: a need rises when its moment comes.
branches.cn: 需求线：需求在时刻到来时升起。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN LINE: appearing and resulting share one upward motion.
branches.cn: 起源线：出现与由原因产生共享同一个向上动作。

intro.en: Arise is an irregular native verb; its forms are listed below with the same root visible in rise.
intro.cn: arise 是本土的不规则动词，下面的条目列出它的各形态，并显示同源的 rise。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin layer here: arise and rise are Germanic words, and Latin has no part in them.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁层：arise 与 rise 都是日耳曼词，拉丁语与此无关。

items.meaning: to come into being or stand up
items.example: Doubt may arise at any stage.
items.exampleCN: 疑问可能在任何阶段出现。
这个问题每年春天都会出现。

items.example: A dispute arose over the land.
items.exampleCN: 围绕着这块地起了争端。

items.example: They discussed the issues arising from the report.
items.exampleCN: 他们讨论了报告中产生的问题。

items.example: The sun rises earlier in June.
The delay arose from a missing form.
items.exampleCN: 延误是由于少了一张表格。

definition_zh: 限度；极限；界限；限制；限定；（口语）令人无法容忍的人或事
definition_en: the greatest amount or level allowed; a boundary; to keep something within a boundary; and, informally, an intolerable person or thing
core_image: 跑道尽头画着一条白线，越过它就算出界
scene: 操场边的公告牌写着每人每天只能领两瓶水，管理员站在桌后一瓶一瓶地数。 The camp set a strict limit on drinking water during the hot week.
sceneCN: 这里是「限度、限额」（第 1 个义项：允许的最大数量）；句意为营地在炎热的一周里给饮用水定了严格限额。图中可辨识物件：公告牌、成排的水瓶、记账的纸单。

pos.zh: 限度；极限；界限；令人无法容忍的人或事

derivatives.zh: 由 limit 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「限制；局限」
由 limit 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无限制的」
由否定前缀 un- 加 limited 构成，义为「无限的；不受限制的」

senses.title: The greatest amount allowed
senses.definition: the largest amount, number or level that is allowed or possible
senses.definitionCN: 被允许或可能达到的最大数量、数目或程度
senses.example: There is a limit to how much I can carry.
senses.exampleCN: 我能搬的东西是有限度的。
senses.why: Latin limes was the path that marked the edge of a field, so a limit began as the line beyond which something stops being allowed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 limes 是标出田地边缘的小路，所以 limit 最初就是「越过就不再被允许」的那条线。

senses.title: A boundary between areas
senses.definition: a line or point marking the edge of an area, beyond which something else begins
senses.definitionCN: 标出某一区域边缘的线或点，越过之后就是别处
senses.example: The river forms the western limit of the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河构成了老城的西界。
senses.why: The same boundary line can be drawn on a map as well as written into a rule, so the physical edge and the allowed amount share one word.
senses.whyCN: 同一条界线既能画在地图上，也能写进规章，所以实体边界与允许量共用一个词。

senses.title: To restrict something
senses.definition: to stop something from growing or going beyond a certain point
senses.definitionCN: 阻止某物继续增长或越过某个点
senses.example: The doctor limited his salt intake to one gram a day.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把他的盐摄入量限制在每天一克。
senses.why: Once a limit is a line, the verb is simply the act of holding things on the near side of that line.
senses.whyCN: 既然 limit 是一条线，动词就是「把事物挡在这条线的近侧」这个动作。

senses.title: An intolerable person or thing
senses.titleCN: 令人无法容忍的人或事（口语）
senses.definition: used in informal speech for a person or thing that is impossible to tolerate
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用来指让人忍无可忍的人或事
senses.example: That child is the limit; he has emptied the whole box.
senses.exampleCN: 那孩子真让人受不了，他把整盒都倒空了。
senses.why: When patience is used up, people say the behaviour has reached the limit, and the phrase then becomes a name for whoever caused it.
senses.whyCN: 耐心被耗尽时，人们说这种行为已经到了极限，这个说法于是直接用来指造成它的人。

intro.en: Limit comes straight from a Latin word for a boundary path, and it has kept the idea of a line ever since.
intro.cn: limit 直接来自一个表示「边界小路」的拉丁词，此后一直保留着「一条线」的意思。

items.en: Limes meant a boundary, a border, or the path that ran along the edge of a field.
items.cn: limes 意为边界、国界，也指标出田地边缘的那条小路。

items.en: The genitive limitis gave the stem limit-, which English kept in every form of the word.
items.cn: 属格 limitis 给出词干 limit-，英语把这个词干保留在这个词的各种形式里。

items.en: The verb limitare meant to mark out a boundary or to set bounds, and it supplied the idea of restricting.
items.cn: 动词 limitare 意为标出边界、设定范围，提供了「加以限制」这一层意思。

items.en: Middle English took limit from French and used it for a boundary or a fixed extent.
items.cn: 中古英语经法语引入 limit，用来指边界或固定的范围。

items.en: Modern English adds the everyday sense of a maximum amount and the informal sense of an intolerable person.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「最大数量」的日常义项，以及「无法容忍的人」这一口语义项。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin boundary stem; the near-meaning group gathers other words for edges and restrictions.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示边界的拉丁词干展开；近义组收表示界线与限制的其他词。

entries.definition: A rule or condition that restricts what is possible.
entries.definitionCN: 限制可能范围的规则或条件。

entries.definition: Having no limit at all.
Not restricted by any limit.
To mark the boundary of something.
A line that marks where an area ends.
The point at which something begins or stops.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物开始或停止的那个点。

entries.definition: An upper limit set on an amount, especially money.
entries.definitionCN: 对数量尤其是金额设定的上限。

entries.definition: A rule that limits what people may do.

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin boundary line, so every hook draws a line and then stands on one side of it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一条拉丁语的边界线，所以每条钩子都先画线，再站到线的一侧。

normal.en: Limes was a path along the edge of a field, so every limit is first a line drawn on the ground.
normal.cn: limes 是沿着田地边缘的小路，所以每个 limit 首先都是画在地上的一条线。

normal.en: The stem limit- never changes: limits, limited and limiting all keep it intact.
normal.cn: 词干 limit- 始终不变：limits、limited、limiting 都完整保留它。

normal.en: Speed limit, time limit and age limit all name the number placed on the far side of the line.
normal.cn: speed limit、time limit、age limit 都是把线另一侧的那个数字说出来。

normal.en: To limit something is to make the line do work, holding growth on the near side.
normal.cn: to limit 某物就是让这条线起作用，把增长挡在近侧。

normal.en: Limitation and limitless take opposite suffixes, -ation and -less, from the same stem.
normal.cn: limitation 与 limitless 在同一词干上加了相反的后缀 -ation 与 -less。

abstract.en: A boundary is useful only because something lies on both sides of it: the word carries the outside with it.
abstract.cn: 边界之所以有用，是因为线两边都有东西：这个词把「外面」也一起带着。

abstract.en: To set a limit is an act of trust in advance, a way of saying how far a relationship will go.
abstract.cn: 设定限度是一种事先的信任，是在说明这层关系能走多远。

abstract.en: When patience runs out, the same word that measured things turns and measures a person.
abstract.cn: 当耐心耗尽，这个原本量事物的词就转过身来量人。

examples.en: There is a limit to how much I can carry.
examples.cn: 我能搬的东西是有限度的。

examples.en: The doctor limited his salt intake to one gram a day.
examples.cn: 医生把他的盐摄入量限制在每天一克。

examples.en: The speed limit on this road is forty.
examples.cn: 这条路的限速是四十。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厘米特」——绳子只到厘米特那么长，再多一厘米就超过限度；limit 是限度。

root: 拉丁语 limes（边界、田边小路），属格 limitis 给出词干 limit-；晚期拉丁语 limitare（划定界限）→ 法语 limite → 英语 limit；同族词多与边界、限制有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a boundary line; the senses divide into the maximum allowed, the geographical edge, the act of restricting, and the point where tolerance runs out.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一条界线」；义项由此分为允许的最大量、地理边界、划线限制的动作，以及耐心到顶时对人的说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white line painted at the end of a running track.
core.cn: 核心意象：跑道尽头画着一条白线，越过它就算出界。

branches.cn: 写着每天两瓶的公告牌

branches.en: a river marking the edge of a town
branches.cn: 标出城镇边缘的一条河

branches.en: a doctor writing a daily maximum
branches.cn: 医生写下的每日上限

branches.cn: 空盒子和疲惫的家长

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun of boundary, its genitive stem and a Late Latin verb of marking bounds.
intro.cn: 这个词依托表示边界的拉丁名词、它的属格词干，以及一个表示划界的晚期拉丁语动词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

latinEntries.meaning: to mark a boundary, to restrict

definition_zh: 外部的；外来的；对外的
definition_en: on or from the outside; coming from another place or group; relating to foreign countries
core_image: 一股来自屋外的风推开窗户
scene: 外部压力迫使公司改变计划。 External pressure forced the company to change its plan.
sceneCN: 这里 external 是「外来的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：外部压力迫使公司改变计划。

senses.title: On the outside
senses.definition: located on or forming the outside of something
senses.definitionCN: 位于外部或构成外部的
senses.example: The external walls are painted white.
senses.exampleCN: 外墙被刷成白色。
senses.why: The core sense is physical position outside.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是位于外部的物理位置。

senses.title: Coming from outside
senses.definition: coming from another place, person, or system
senses.definitionCN: 来自其他地方、人或系统的
senses.example: External pressure changed the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 外部压力改变了决定。
senses.why: Position becomes the source of influence.
senses.whyCN: 位置变成影响的来源。

senses.title: Relating to foreign affairs
senses.definition: relating to relations with other countries
senses.definitionCN: 与别国关系有关的
senses.example: He works in external affairs.
senses.exampleCN: 他从事对外事务。
senses.why: The outside of a country is the foreign world.
senses.whyCN: 一个国家的「外部」就是外国世界。

intro.en: External comes from Latin externus, from exterus, meaning outward.
intro.cn: external 来自拉丁语 externus，根源是 exterus（向外的）。

items.en: Exterus means outward or foreign.
items.cn: exterus 意为向外的或外来的。

items.en: Externus means belonging to the outside.
items.cn: externus 意为属于外部的。

items.en: The word contrasts with internus, inner.
items.cn: 这个词与表示内部的 internus 相对。

items.en: External names what lies outside a system.
items.cn: external 指位于系统之外的事物。

items.en: External covers foreign affairs and devices.
items.cn: 现代英语中 external 涵盖对外事务与外接设备。

note.en: External is outside; internal is inside.
note.cn: external 是外部的，internal 则是内部的。

inside something

farther from the center

normalIntro.en: External marks what is outside a person, system, or country.
normalIntro.cn: external 标记人或系统、国家之外的事物。

normal.en: External doors must be locked at night.
normal.cn: 外门夜间必须上锁。

normal.en: The company faced strong external pressure.
normal.cn: 公司面临强大的外部压力。

normal.en: An external drive stores extra files.
normal.cn: 外置硬盘用来存放额外文件。

normal.en: The medicine is for external use only.
normal.cn: 这种药仅供外用。

normal.en: External factors slowed the economy.
normal.cn: 外部因素让经济放缓。

abstract.en: Picture wind pushing a window open from outside.
abstract.cn: 想象风从外面把窗户吹开。

abstract.en: Imagine a voice entering a quiet room through the door.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音从门缝进入安静的房间。

abstract.en: Think of a country looking outward across its border.
abstract.cn: 想象一个国家越过边界向外看。

examples.en: External pressure forced the manager to resign.
examples.cn: 外部压力迫使经理辞职。

examples.en: The external surface is rough and cold.
examples.cn: 外表面粗糙而冰冷。

examples.en: The country changed its external policy.
examples.cn: 这个国家改变了对外政策。

dict_mnemonic.text: extern 表示「外部」，加形容词后缀 -al，就是 external（外部的）。

root: 源自拉丁语 externus（外部的），由 exterus（向外的）派生，核心义「位于或来自外部」。

sensesIntro.en: External means on the outside, coming from outside, or relating to foreign affairs.
sensesIntro.cn: external 意为位于外部、来自外部，或与对外事务有关。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wind entering from outside a room.
core.cn: 核心意象：从屋外进入房间的风。

branches.en: The base sense is physical position outside.
branches.cn: 基础义是外部的物理位置。

branches.en: Position becomes the source of influence.
branches.cn: 位置变成影响的来源。

branches.en: The outside of a country is the foreign world.
branches.cn: 国家的「外部」就是外国世界。

branches.en: Outer walls and outside pressure share the same boundary.
branches.cn: 外墙与外部压力共享同一条边界。

branches.en: Outside forces and foreign affairs both cross a border.
branches.cn: 外部力量与对外事务都越过边界。

intro.en: External is exterus plus -al, and it belongs with exterior and extreme.
intro.cn: external 由 exterus 加 -al 构成，与 exterior、extreme 同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin externus, exterus, and the suffix -alis are the source elements.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 externus、exterus 与词尾 -alis 是来源要素。

items.example: She externalized her feelings in a letter.
items.exampleCN: 她在信里把感情表达出来。
污染是典型的外部性问题。

items.example: The exterior is made of brick.
Internal doors are made of wood.
